papers_seen.author: Hicks
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Adaptation: Teaching to Adapt
papers_seen.abstract: Domain adaptation is crucial in many real-world applications where the distribution of the training data differs from the distribution of the test data. Previous Deep Learning-based approaches to domain adaptation need to be trained jointly on source and target domain data and are therefore unappealing in scenarios where models need to be adapted to a large number of domains or where a domain is evolving, e.g. spam detection where attackers continuously change their tactics.   To fill this gap, we propose Knowledge Adaptation, an extension of Knowledge Distillation (Bucilua et al., 2006; Hinton et al., 2015) to the domain adaptation scenario. We show how a student model achieves state-of-the-art results on unsupervised domain adaptation from multiple sources on a standard sentiment analysis benchmark by taking into account the domain-specific expertise of multiple teachers and the similarities between their domains.   When learning from a single teacher, using domain similarity to gauge trustworthiness is inadequate. To this end, we propose a simple metric that correlates well with the teacher's accuracy in the target domain. We demonstrate that incorporating high-confidence examples selected by this metric enables the student model to achieve state-of-the-art performance in the single-source scenario.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Davidson
papers_seen.title: Robust Re-Identification by Multiple Views Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: To achieve robustness in Re-Identification, standard methods leverage tracking information in a Video-To-Video fashion. However, these solutions face a large drop in performance for single image queries (e.g., Image-To-Video setting). Recent works address this severe degradation by transferring temporal information from a Video-based network to an Image-based one. In this work, we devise a training strategy that allows the transfer of a superior knowledge, arising from a set of views depicting the target object. Our proposal - Views Knowledge Distillation (VKD) - pins this visual variety as a supervision signal within a teacher-student framework, where the teacher educates a student who observes fewer views. As a result, the student outperforms not only its teacher but also the current state-of-the-art in Image-To-Video by a wide margin (6.3% mAP on MARS, 8.6% on Duke-Video-ReId and 5% on VeRi-776). A thorough analysis - on Person, Vehicle and Animal Re-ID - investigates the properties of VKD from a qualitatively and quantitatively perspective. Code is available at https://github.com/aimagelab/VKD.

papers_seen.abstract: Spoken question answering (SQA) is a challenging task that requires the machine to fully understand the complex spoken documents. To address the issue, we present a novel distillation framework. Specifically, we devise a training strategy to perform knowledge distillation (KD) from spoken documents and written counterparts. Our work makes a step towards distilling knowledge from the language model as a supervision signal to lead to better student accuracy by reducing the misalignment between automatic and manual transcriptions. Experiments demonstrate that our approach outperforms several state-of-the-art language models on the Spoken-SQuAD dataset.

papers_seen.author: Herrera
papers_seen.title: Compressing GANs using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been used in several machine learning tasks such as domain transfer, super resolution, and synthetic data generation. State-of-the-art GANs often use tens of millions of parameters, making them expensive to deploy for applications in low SWAP (size, weight, and power) hardware, such as mobile devices, and for applications with real time capabilities. There has been no work found to reduce the number of parameters used in GANs. Therefore, we propose a method to compress GANs using knowledge distillation techniques, in which a smaller "student" GAN learns to mimic a larger "teacher" GAN. We show that the distillation methods used on MNIST, CIFAR-10, and Celeb-A datasets can compress teacher GANs at ratios of 1669:1, 58:1, and 87:1, respectively, while retaining the quality of the generated image. From our experiments, we observe a qualitative limit for GAN's compression. Moreover, we observe that, with a fixed parameter budget, compressed GANs outperform GANs trained using standard training methods. We conjecture that this is partially owing to the optimization landscape of over-parameterized GANs which allows efficient training using alternating gradient descent. Thus, training an over-parameterized GAN followed by our proposed compression scheme provides a high quality generative model with a small number of parameters.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create compact and efficient neural networks. This technique involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, this approach reduces computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning, using a range of methods from mimicking output probabilities to distilling internal representations and employing adversarial learning frameworks.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions and internal representations to the student. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and distributed learning, spanning domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Stewart
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. While initially conceived to create lightweight networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used to improve model robustness against adversarial attacks, transfer knowledge between different model architectures, and facilitate complex learning paradigms such as federated and continual learning. This technique has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, demonstrating its flexibility and broad utility beyond simple compression.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful machine learning technique for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core idea is to transfer the generalized knowledge learned by the teacher, which is often encoded in its output probabilities, to the student. This allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices or applications with strict latency requirements. The applications of knowledge distillation are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning. Beyond simple model compression, distillation has been shown to improve the accuracy of student models, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable training even when the original data is unavailable.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.author: Collins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, complex deep learning models into smaller, more efficient counterparts. This process involves a "teacher-student" paradigm, where a smaller student network learns to mimic the outputs or internal representations of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable performance while significantly reducing computational and memory requirements. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as on mobile devices or for latency-sensitive applications. The applications of knowledge distillation are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where it is used to create compact language models, and computer vision, for tasks like object detection and image classification. Research continues to explore novel distillation methods, including data-free approaches and cross-architecture knowledge transfer, further enhancing its flexibility and effectiveness.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: Less is More: Task-aware Layer-wise Distillation for Language Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Layer-wise distillation is a powerful tool to compress large models (i.e. teacher models) into small ones (i.e., student models). The student distills knowledge from the teacher by mimicking the hidden representations of the teacher at every intermediate layer. However, layer-wise distillation is difficult. Since the student has a smaller model capacity than the teacher, it is often under-fitted. Furthermore, the hidden representations of the teacher contain redundant information that the student does not necessarily need for the target task's learning. To address these challenges, we propose a novel Task-aware layEr-wise Distillation (TED). TED designs task-aware filters to align the hidden representations of the student and the teacher at each layer. The filters select the knowledge that is useful for the target task from the hidden representations. As such, TED reduces the knowledge gap between the two models and helps the student to fit better on the target task. We evaluate TED in two scenarios: continual pre-training and fine-tuning. TED demonstrates significant and consistent improvements over existing distillation methods in both scenarios. Code is available at https://github.com/cliang1453/task-aware-distillation.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: MEAL: Multi-Model Ensemble via Adversarial Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Often the best performing deep neural models are ensembles of multiple base-level networks. Unfortunately, the space required to store these many networks, and the time required to execute them at test-time, prohibits their use in applications where test sets are large (e.g., ImageNet). In this paper, we present a method for compressing large, complex trained ensembles into a single network, where knowledge from a variety of trained deep neural networks (DNNs) is distilled and transferred to a single DNN. In order to distill diverse knowledge from different trained (teacher) models, we propose to use adversarial-based learning strategy where we define a block-wise training loss to guide and optimize the predefined student network to recover the knowledge in teacher models, and to promote the discriminator network to distinguish teacher vs. student features simultaneously. The proposed ensemble method (MEAL) of transferring distilled knowledge with adversarial learning exhibits three important advantages: (1) the student network that learns the distilled knowledge with discriminators is optimized better than the original model; (2) fast inference is realized by a single forward pass, while the performance is even better than traditional ensembles from multi-original models; (3) the student network can learn the distilled knowledge from a teacher model that has arbitrary structures. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, SVHN and ImageNet datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our MEAL method. On ImageNet, our ResNet-50 based MEAL achieves top-1/5 21.79%/5.99% val error, which outperforms the original model by 2.06%/1.14%. Code and models are available at: https://github.com/AaronHeee/MEAL

papers_seen.title: Multi-Label Image Classification via Knowledge Distillation from Weakly-Supervised Detection
papers_seen.abstract: Multi-label image classification is a fundamental but challenging task towards general visual understanding. Existing methods found the region-level cues (e.g., features from RoIs) can facilitate multi-label classification. Nevertheless, such methods usually require laborious object-level annotations (i.e., object labels and bounding boxes) for effective learning of the object-level visual features. In this paper, we propose a novel and efficient deep framework to boost multi-label classification by distilling knowledge from weakly-supervised detection task without bounding box annotations. Specifically, given the image-level annotations, (1) we first develop a weakly-supervised detection (WSD) model, and then (2) construct an end-to-end multi-label image classification framework augmented by a knowledge distillation module that guides the classification model by the WSD model according to the class-level predictions for the whole image and the object-level visual features for object RoIs. The WSD model is the teacher model and the classification model is the student model. After this cross-task knowledge distillation, the performance of the classification model is significantly improved and the efficiency is maintained since the WSD model can be safely discarded in the test phase. Extensive experiments on two large-scale datasets (MS-COCO and NUS-WIDE) show that our framework achieves superior performances over the state-of-the-art methods on both performance and efficiency.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Shaffer
papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: Is Label Smoothing Truly Incompatible with Knowledge Distillation: An Empirical Study
papers_seen.abstract: This work aims to empirically clarify a recently discovered perspective that label smoothing is incompatible with knowledge distillation. We begin by introducing the motivation behind on how this incompatibility is raised, i.e., label smoothing erases relative information between teacher logits. We provide a novel connection on how label smoothing affects distributions of semantically similar and dissimilar classes. Then we propose a metric to quantitatively measure the degree of erased information in sample's representation. After that, we study its one-sidedness and imperfection of the incompatibility view through massive analyses, visualizations and comprehensive experiments on Image Classification, Binary Networks, and Neural Machine Translation. Finally, we broadly discuss several circumstances wherein label smoothing will indeed lose its effectiveness. Project page: http://zhiqiangshen.com/projects/LS_and_KD/index.html.

papers_seen.author: Ware
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their large size and computational demands often hinder practical deployment. Model compression techniques are crucial for addressing this challenge, with knowledge distillation emerging as a particularly effective and versatile framework. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. By training the student to mimic the teacher's behavior, it is possible to create compact models that retain a high level of performance while being significantly faster and less resource-intensive. The utility of this approach extends beyond simple compression, as it can also be used to enhance model performance and robustness. Knowledge distillation has proven successful across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it an indispensable tool for bridging the gap between state-of-the-art research and real-world applications.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions without a significant loss in performance. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, a compact student model learns to mimic the behavior of a larger teacher model, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. While model compression is its primary application, the utility of knowledge distillation extends much further. The framework has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, facilitate knowledge transfer across different tasks, and address challenges in data privacy and continual learning, establishing it as a multifaceted and foundational tool in modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Coleman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful neural networks on devices with limited computational resources, such as mobile phones. While its primary goal is to reduce model size and latency, the applications of knowledge distillation extend further, serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning strategies in areas like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process serves a dual purpose: it facilitates model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, and it often enhances the performance and generalization capabilities of the student model beyond what could be achieved through standard training. Its applications are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, proving to be a flexible and powerful tool for optimizing deep neural networks for practical use.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Mitchell

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used in deep learning to create smaller, more efficient models. The technique is versatile, with applications across various domains including natural language processing and computer vision, and is also used to enhance model performance and address other challenges like domain adaptation.

papers_seen.author: Cobb
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create efficient, lightweight deep learning models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior and knowledge of a larger, more powerful "teacher" model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Methodologies for knowledge transfer have evolved from matching output probabilities to more advanced techniques that focus on intermediate feature representations. This versatile technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including computer vision, natural language processing, and graph-based learning, demonstrating its effectiveness beyond simple compression to enhance overall model performance.

papers_seen.author: Nolan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique in deep learning, designed to address the challenges of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments. papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is widely recognized as a powerful model compression technique in deep learning, designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, cumbersome ones. This process involves a 'teacher-student' framework where a compact student model learns to mimic the rich outputs of a pre-trained teacher. While its primary application is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple size reduction. It has evolved into a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and increasing model interpretability. Furthermore, advanced distillation methods can facilitate knowledge transfer in challenging scenarios, such as when the original training data is unavailable. This multifaceted capability establishes knowledge distillation not just as a compression tool, but as a fundamental paradigm for developing more practical, adaptable, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Deleon
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to address this issue. In this paradigm, a smaller 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of lightweight yet powerful models that are faster and more efficient at inference. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation has demonstrated the ability to enhance student model performance, improve robustness, and mitigate undesirable biases. As a flexible and multifaceted framework, it serves as a crucial tool for making state-of-the-art deep learning models practical for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Walters
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. The process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of high-performing neural networks in resource-constrained environments. This is achieved by transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions and internal representations to the student. The applications of this versatile framework are broad, extending beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and distributed learning, spanning domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Cowan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the "teacher," to a smaller, more efficient model, the "student." This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and inference latency without a significant loss in performance. The core idea involves training the student model to mimic the output distributions of the teacher model, effectively learning a richer, more generalized representation than it could from ground-truth labels alone. This technique has found broad applications across various domains, including Natural Language Processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. Research explores not only compressing models but also enhancing their performance, adapting them for multi-task learning, and enabling privacy-preserving or distributed learning paradigms.

While its primary goal is size reduction, the applications of this versatile paradigm have expanded to include performance enhancement, robustness improvement, and enabling complex learning scenarios across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used in deep learning and natural language processing to address the challenge of deploying large models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often through its soft predictions or internal representations, to the more compact student network. While its primary goal is to create smaller and faster models that maintain high performance, the versatility of knowledge distillation also allows it to be used for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling novel learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Martin
papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.author: Webster
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of modern deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a highly effective model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, the student can achieve high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. Initially developed for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, making it a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms. This process successfully bridges the gap between state-of-the-art performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Rios
papers_seen.title: Improving Neural Topic Models using Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Topic models are often used to identify human-interpretable topics to help make sense of large document collections. We use knowledge distillation to combine the best attributes of probabilistic topic models and pretrained transformers. Our modular method can be straightforwardly applied with any neural topic model to improve topic quality, which we demonstrate using two models having disparate architectures, obtaining state-of-the-art topic coherence. We show that our adaptable framework not only improves performance in the aggregate over all estimated topics, as is commonly reported, but also in head-to-head comparisons of aligned topics.

The framework is now widely used to enhance student model performance, preserve data privacy in distributed learning settings, mitigate algorithmic bias, and transfer knowledge in data-scarce scenarios. This versatility establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for creating more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Wheeler
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process enables the deployment of high-performing deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. The fundamental approach involves training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs, but numerous variations have been developed to enhance this process. These include distilling knowledge from intermediate feature representations, using multiple teachers for domain adaptation or multi-task learning, and applying distillation in specialized areas like object detection and graph neural networks. Advanced methods address challenges such as the absence of training data, the propagation of model biases, and applications in privacy-preserving federated learning. By leveraging knowledge from more capable models, distillation significantly improves the performance of compact networks across a wide range of tasks in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Welch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for compressing large, state-of-the-art deep learning models into smaller, more efficient versions suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve performance far exceeding what it could by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven effective across a wide array of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and speech recognition, enabling the practical application of otherwise computationally prohibitive models. The methodology extends beyond simple output imitation, with advanced techniques focusing on transferring internal representations and adapting the teaching process itself to further enhance student performance and generalization.

papers_seen.author: Harris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale deep learning models have achieved state-of-the-art performance on many tasks but their size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, offer a solution by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a high degree of the teacher's performance. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, to develop smaller, domain-specific language models, improve machine translation systems, and compress complex ensemble models. Research has also explored its use in mitigating societal biases in language models. The versatility of this technique is further demonstrated by different approaches, such as self-distillation and data-free distillation, which expand its applicability. The success of knowledge distillation is often attributed to the rich, supervisory information contained in the teacher's soft probability outputs and its ability to act as a form of learned regularization.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process allows the student model to inherit the rich knowledge of the teacher, often achieving performance superior to what it could attain through standard training. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, improved generalization, and knowledge transfer across diverse architectures and domains.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process aims to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational cost. The transfer can occur through various means, including mimicking the teacher's output probabilities or its internal feature representations. Advanced methods have emerged, such as online distillation where models teach each other, and meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its training strategy to better instruct the student. This technique has found broad applications in both natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the deployment of sophisticated models in resource-constrained environments by creating efficient, task-specific networks for tasks ranging from language understanding to 3D object detection.

papers_seen.author: Munoz
papers_seen.title: Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation in Deep Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation deals with the problem of training a smaller model (Student) from a high capacity source model (Teacher) so as to retain most of its performance. Existing approaches use either the training data or meta-data extracted from it in order to train the Student. However, accessing the dataset on which the Teacher has been trained may not always be feasible if the dataset is very large or it poses privacy or safety concerns (e.g., bio-metric or medical data). Hence, in this paper, we propose a novel data-free method to train the Student from the Teacher. Without even using any meta-data, we synthesize the Data Impressions from the complex Teacher model and utilize these as surrogates for the original training data samples to transfer its learning to Student via knowledge distillation. We, therefore, dub our method "Zero-Shot Knowledge Distillation" and demonstrate that our framework results in competitive generalization performance as achieved by distillation using the actual training data samples on multiple benchmark datasets.

papers_seen.title: Towards Practical Lipreading with Distilled and Efficient Models
papers_seen.abstract: Lipreading has witnessed a lot of progress due to the resurgence of neural networks. Recent works have placed emphasis on aspects such as improving performance by finding the optimal architecture or improving generalization. However, there is still a significant gap between the current methodologies and the requirements for an effective deployment of lipreading in practical scenarios. In this work, we propose a series of innovations that significantly bridge that gap: first, we raise the state-of-the-art performance by a wide margin on LRW and LRW-1000 to 88.5% and 46.6%, respectively using self-distillation. Secondly, we propose a series of architectural changes, including a novel Depthwise Separable Temporal Convolutional Network (DS-TCN) head, that slashes the computational cost to a fraction of the (already quite efficient) original model. Thirdly, we show that knowledge distillation is a very effective tool for recovering performance of the lightweight models. This results in a range of models with different accuracy-efficiency trade-offs. However, our most promising lightweight models are on par with the current state-of-the-art while showing a reduction of 8.2x and 3.9x in terms of computational cost and number of parameters, respectively, which we hope will enable the deployment of lipreading models in practical applications.

papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge from Deep Networks with Applications to Healthcare Domain
papers_seen.abstract: Exponential growth in Electronic Healthcare Records (EHR) has resulted in new opportunities and urgent needs for discovery of meaningful data-driven representations and patterns of diseases in Computational Phenotyping research. Deep Learning models have shown superior performance for robust prediction in computational phenotyping tasks, but suffer from the issue of model interpretability which is crucial for clinicians involved in decision-making. In this paper, we introduce a novel knowledge-distillation approach called Interpretable Mimic Learning, to learn interpretable phenotype features for making robust prediction while mimicking the performance of deep learning models. Our framework uses Gradient Boosting Trees to learn interpretable features from deep learning models such as Stacked Denoising Autoencoder and Long Short-Term Memory. Exhaustive experiments on a real-world clinical time-series dataset show that our method obtains similar or better performance than the deep learning models, and it provides interpretable phenotypes for clinical decision making.

papers_seen.title: Federated Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Distributed learning frameworks often rely on exchanging model parameters across workers, instead of revealing their raw data. A prime example is federated learning that exchanges the gradients or weights of each neural network model. Under limited communication resources, however, such a method becomes extremely costly particularly for modern deep neural networks having a huge number of model parameters. In this regard, federated distillation (FD) is a compelling distributed learning solution that only exchanges the model outputs whose dimensions are commonly much smaller than the model sizes (e.g., 10 labels in the MNIST dataset). The goal of this chapter is to provide a deep understanding of FD while demonstrating its communication efficiency and applicability to a variety of tasks. To this end, towards demystifying the operational principle of FD, the first part of this chapter provides a novel asymptotic analysis for two foundational algorithms of FD, namely knowledge distillation (KD) and co-distillation (CD), by exploiting the theory of neural tangent kernel (NTK). Next, the second part elaborates on a baseline implementation of FD for a classification task, and illustrates its performance in terms of accuracy and communication efficiency compared to FL. Lastly, to demonstrate the applicability of FD to various distributed learning tasks and environments, the third part presents two selected applications, namely FD over asymmetric uplink-and-downlink wireless channels and FD for reinforcement learning.

papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their immense size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, especially knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution to this problem. Knowledge distillation is a process where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This allows the student to learn a compressed representation of the teacher's knowledge, resulting in a much smaller and faster model that retains a high level of performance. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a highly effective and versatile framework for compressing deep learning models, enabling their practical application in diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. By leveraging knowledge from a powerful but cumbersome teacher, distillation produces efficient student models that bridge the gap between high performance and practical deployability.

papers_seen.author: Alvarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing complexity of deep learning models has created significant challenges for their deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible model compression technique to address this issue. This method involves training a compact 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, effectively transferring its learned knowledge. This process enables the creation of smaller, faster models that retain high performance, making them suitable for practical applications. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its successful application across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning, as well as in specialized contexts like data-free learning and enhancing model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Pennington
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art networks, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. While its principal application is compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded, serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating knowledge transfer across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The versatility of this framework has led to its successful application across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its use cases extend beyond compression to performance enhancement and knowledge transfer.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Oliver
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model, enabling the deployment of powerful but computationally expensive networks in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. The student learns from the rich, generalized information encoded in the teacher's outputs, often achieving higher performance than if trained on ground-truth labels alone. Initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a versatile framework used not only for compression but also to enhance model performance, robustness, and generalization across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Lee
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm where a smaller 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more powerful 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing their computational and memory footprints. The core principle involves transferring the generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, often using the teacher's output probabilities as soft labels. The applications of this technique have expanded beyond simple compression to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling novel learning scenarios like data-free training and federated learning across heterogeneous devices.

It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. While initially conceived for creating lightweight models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, proving its versatility for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer across different architectures and domains.

papers_seen.author: Walls
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to deploy high-performing models on resource-constrained devices by reducing their size and computational cost. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to improving performance in tasks like neural machine translation, graph-based learning, and recommender systems. Variations of the technique leverage multiple teachers, adversarial samples, and feature-based mimicry to enhance the student model's capabilities, sometimes even allowing the student to surpass the performance of its teacher.

This teacher-student framework enables the deployment of powerful neural network architectures in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, by creating compact models that retain high performance. Beyond its primary application in compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile paradigm for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios. This approach has found broad applicability across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, making it a crucial tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cohen
papers_seen.title: ALP-KD: Attention-Based Layer Projection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is considered as a training and compression strategy in which two neural networks, namely a teacher and a student, are coupled together during training. The teacher network is supposed to be a trustworthy predictor and the student tries to mimic its predictions. Usually, a student with a lighter architecture is selected so we can achieve compression and yet deliver high-quality results. In such a setting, distillation only happens for final predictions whereas the student could also benefit from teacher's supervision for internal components.   Motivated by this, we studied the problem of distillation for intermediate layers. Since there might not be a one-to-one alignment between student and teacher layers, existing techniques skip some teacher layers and only distill from a subset of them. This shortcoming directly impacts quality, so we instead propose a combinatorial technique which relies on attention. Our model fuses teacher-side information and takes each layer's significance into consideration, then performs distillation between combined teacher layers and those of the student. Using our technique, we distilled a 12-layer BERT (Devlin et al. 2019) into 6-, 4-, and 2-layer counterparts and evaluated them on GLUE tasks (Wang et al. 2018). Experimental results show that our combinatorial approach is able to outperform other existing techniques.

papers_seen.abstract: State-of-the-art CNN based recognition models are often computationally prohibitive to deploy on low-end devices. A promising high level approach tackling this limitation is knowledge distillation, which let small student model mimic cumbersome teacher model's output to get improved generalization. However, related methods mainly focus on simple task of classification while do not consider complex tasks like object detection. We show applying the vanilla knowledge distillation to detection model gets minor gain. To address the challenge of distilling knowledge in detection model, we propose a fine-grained feature imitation method exploiting the cross-location discrepancy of feature response. Our intuition is that detectors care more about local near object regions. Thus the discrepancy of feature response on the near object anchor locations reveals important information of how teacher model tends to generalize. We design a novel mechanism to estimate those locations and let student model imitate the teacher on them to get enhanced performance. We first validate the idea on a developed lightweight toy detector which carries simplest notion of current state-of-the-art anchor based detection models on challenging KITTI dataset, our method generates up to 15% boost of mAP for the student model compared to the non-imitated counterpart. We then extensively evaluate the method with Faster R-CNN model under various scenarios with common object detection benchmark of Pascal VOC and COCO, imitation alleviates up to 74% performance drop of student model compared to teacher. Codes released at https://github.com/twangnh/Distilling-Object-Detectors

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a versatile technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process involves a compact 'student' model being trained to mimic the behavior of a pre-trained, cumbersome 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to retain the high performance of the teacher while reducing computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of advanced models on resource-constrained devices. However, the applications and implications of knowledge distillation extend far beyond simple compression. It serves as a powerful framework for knowledge transfer, performance enhancement, and addressing ethical considerations like fairness, making it a fundamental tool for creating more practical and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.title: Selective Knowledge Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Neural Machine Translation (NMT) models achieve state-of-the-art performance on many translation benchmarks. As an active research field in NMT, knowledge distillation is widely applied to enhance the model's performance by transferring teacher model's knowledge on each training sample. However, previous work rarely discusses the different impacts and connections among these samples, which serve as the medium for transferring teacher knowledge. In this paper, we design a novel protocol that can effectively analyze the different impacts of samples by comparing various samples' partitions. Based on above protocol, we conduct extensive experiments and find that the teacher's knowledge is not the more, the better. Knowledge over specific samples may even hurt the whole performance of knowledge distillation. Finally, to address these issues, we propose two simple yet effective strategies, i.e., batch-level and global-level selections, to pick suitable samples for distillation. We evaluate our approaches on two large-scale machine translation tasks, WMT'14 English->German and WMT'19 Chinese->English. Experimental results show that our approaches yield up to +1.28 and +0.89 BLEU points improvements over the Transformer baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.author: Santos
papers_seen.title: Channel Distillation: Channel-Wise Attention for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is to transfer the knowledge from the data learned by the teacher network to the student network, so that the student has the advantage of less parameters and less calculations, and the accuracy is close to the teacher. In this paper, we propose a new distillation method, which contains two transfer distillation strategies and a loss decay strategy. The first transfer strategy is based on channel-wise attention, called Channel Distillation (CD). CD transfers the channel information from the teacher to the student. The second is Guided Knowledge Distillation (GKD). Unlike Knowledge Distillation (KD), which allows the student to mimic each sample's prediction distribution of the teacher, GKD only enables the student to mimic the correct output of the teacher. The last part is Early Decay Teacher (EDT). During the training process, we gradually decay the weight of the distillation loss. The purpose is to enable the student to gradually control the optimization rather than the teacher. Our proposed method is evaluated on ImageNet and CIFAR100. On ImageNet, we achieve 27.68% of top-1 error with ResNet18, which outperforms state-of-the-art methods. On CIFAR100, we achieve surprising result that the student outperforms the teacher. Code is available at https://github.com/zhouzaida/channel-distillation.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. This is achieved through a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and knowledge of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. While the primary goal is to enable the deployment of complex models on resource-constrained devices, the applications of knowledge distillation extend much further. The technique has been shown to enhance the performance and generalization of student models, and it serves as a flexible framework for transferring desirable properties. Its utility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a multifaceted tool for improving model robustness, enabling multi-task learning, and facilitating domain adaptation, positioning it as a fundamental paradigm for making advanced artificial intelligence more practical and capable.

papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

The technique operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high accuracy with a significantly smaller computational footprint. While initially developed for creating compact and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly, proving its versatility for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring complex capabilities across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Flynn
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, facilitating their deployment on resource-constrained devices. This method has been successfully applied across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation also serves to enhance student model performance and has been adapted to address other objectives such as improving interpretability, privacy, and algorithmic fairness.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to create smaller, more efficient deep learning models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's outputs or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable accuracy with significantly lower computational and memory requirements. This versatile technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the practical application of state-of-the-art models.

papers_seen.author: Johnson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Wide Neural Networks: Risk Bound, Data Efficiency and Imperfect Teacher
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a strategy of training a student network with guide of the soft output from a teacher network. It has been a successful method of model compression and knowledge transfer. However, currently knowledge distillation lacks a convincing theoretical understanding. On the other hand, recent finding on neural tangent kernel enables us to approximate a wide neural network with a linear model of the network's random features. In this paper, we theoretically analyze the knowledge distillation of a wide neural network. First we provide a transfer risk bound for the linearized model of the network. Then we propose a metric of the task's training difficulty, called data inefficiency. Based on this metric, we show that for a perfect teacher, a high ratio of teacher's soft labels can be beneficial. Finally, for the case of imperfect teacher, we find that hard labels can correct teacher's wrong prediction, which explains the practice of mixing hard and soft labels.

papers_seen.author: Morales
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to create lightweight models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in performance. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy while maintaining a small computational footprint. The applications of this framework, however, extend far beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and knowledge transfer across different tasks and domains, making it a multifaceted tool in modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, while powerful, are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to overcome this limitation. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that maintain high performance with significantly reduced computational and memory requirements. This versatile framework facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments and has expanded to applications beyond compression, including performance enhancement and improving model fairness.

papers_seen.author: Young
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Technique for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for transferring knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process serves a dual purpose: it facilitates model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, and it often enhances the performance and generalization capabilities of the student model beyond what could be achieved through standard training. Its applications are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, proving to be a flexible and powerful tool for optimizing deep neural networks for practical use.

papers_seen.author: Hickman
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Strategy for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world, resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques have emerged as a critical field of study to address these issues. Knowledge distillation, a prominent compression method, involves training a smaller 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student model to achieve performance far exceeding what it could attain by training on ground-truth labels alone. This approach has proven versatile, with applications spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, leading to models that are not only smaller and faster but also maintain high levels of accuracy, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art deep learning.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Explaining Knowledge Distillation by Quantifying the Knowledge
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a method to interpret the success of knowledge distillation by quantifying and analyzing task-relevant and task-irrelevant visual concepts that are encoded in intermediate layers of a deep neural network (DNN). More specifically, three hypotheses are proposed as follows. 1. Knowledge distillation makes the DNN learn more visual concepts than learning from raw data. 2. Knowledge distillation ensures that the DNN is prone to learning various visual concepts simultaneously. Whereas, in the scenario of learning from raw data, the DNN learns visual concepts sequentially. 3. Knowledge distillation yields more stable optimization directions than learning from raw data. Accordingly, we design three types of mathematical metrics to evaluate feature representations of the DNN. In experiments, we diagnosed various DNNs, and above hypotheses were verified.

papers_seen.author: Garcia
papers_seen.title: Compressing Visual-linguistic Model via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite exciting progress in pre-training for visual-linguistic (VL) representations, very few aspire to a small VL model. In this paper, we study knowledge distillation (KD) to effectively compress a transformer-based large VL model into a small VL model. The major challenge arises from the inconsistent regional visual tokens extracted from different detectors of Teacher and Student, resulting in the misalignment of hidden representations and attention distributions. To address the problem, we retrain and adapt the Teacher by using the same region proposals from Student's detector while the features are from Teacher's own object detector. With aligned network inputs, the adapted Teacher is capable of transferring the knowledge through the intermediate representations. Specifically, we use the mean square error loss to mimic the attention distribution inside the transformer block and present a token-wise noise contrastive loss to align the hidden state by contrasting with negative representations stored in a sample queue. To this end, we show that our proposed distillation significantly improves the performance of small VL models on image captioning and visual question answering tasks. It reaches 120.8 in CIDEr score on COCO captioning, an improvement of 5.1 over its non-distilled counterpart; and an accuracy of 69.8 on VQA 2.0, a 0.8 gain from the baseline. Our extensive experiments and ablations confirm the effectiveness of VL distillation in both pre-training and fine-tuning stages.
