papers_seen.author: Ray
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models without significant performance degradation. The process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This knowledge transfer allows for the deployment of complex neural networks on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones. While primarily used for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving fairness and interpretability, and enabling complex learning paradigms like federated learning. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, most notably in Natural Language Processing (NLP) for compressing large language models and in computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Diaz
papers_seen.title: Model Compression with Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation for Web Question Answering System
papers_seen.abstract: Deep pre-training and fine-tuning models (such as BERT and OpenAI GPT) have demonstrated excellent results in question answering areas. However, due to the sheer amount of model parameters, the inference speed of these models is very slow. How to apply these complex models to real business scenarios becomes a challenging but practical problem. Previous model compression methods usually suffer from information loss during the model compression procedure, leading to inferior models compared with the original one. To tackle this challenge, we propose a Two-stage Multi-teacher Knowledge Distillation (TMKD for short) method for web Question Answering system. We first develop a general Q\&A distillation task for student model pre-training, and further fine-tune this pre-trained student model with multi-teacher knowledge distillation on downstream tasks (like Web Q\&A task, MNLI, SNLI, RTE tasks from GLUE), which effectively reduces the overfitting bias in individual teacher models, and transfers more general knowledge to the student model. The experiment results show that our method can significantly outperform the baseline methods and even achieve comparable results with the original teacher models, along with substantial speedup of model inference.

papers_seen.author: Obrien
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The student model is trained to mimic the behavior of the teacher, leveraging the rich, generalized information contained in its predictions or internal representations. While primarily used for reducing computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, enabling domain adaptation, and facilitating privacy-preserving learning.

papers_seen.author: Higgins
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective Technique for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: As deep learning models grow in size and complexity, their deployment in resource-constrained environments becomes a significant challenge. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, faster, and more efficient models without substantial performance degradation. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful paradigm for this purpose. It involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller 'student' model. The student learns to mimic the rich output distributions of the teacher, thereby inheriting its performance capabilities while maintaining a much smaller footprint. This approach has proven effective across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, enabling the use of state-of-the-art architectures in practical, real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: King
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process involves training a smaller, efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is to transfer the teacher's knowledge, enabling the creation of compact models that maintain high performance while reducing computational and memory demands. This facilitates the deployment of advanced AI on resource-constrained devices. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, improved generalization, and enabling complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Koch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prevalent model compression technique designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and memory requirements for deployment while maintaining high performance. This process is achieved through various methods, including mimicking the teacher's output predictions, intermediate feature representations, or latent knowledge structures. Research in this area has expanded to address advanced scenarios such as handling exceptionally strong teachers, training teachers to be more effective for distillation, and performing distillation without access to the original training data. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a versatile and effective technique, with successful applications across diverse fields including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and medical imaging.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, the student model can achieve high accuracy with a reduced computational and memory footprint. However, the utility of this framework extends far beyond simple compression, with applications in enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms, making it a critical tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

The primary objective is to create smaller, more computationally efficient models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student to replicate the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its broad application and its evolution into more advanced methods, including data-free distillation and self-distillation, which extend its utility beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and improved generalization.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models in Natural Language Processing (NLP), have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and slow for practical deployment. Model compression techniques are essential for creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression paradigm where a compact "student" model learns from a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. This process involves transferring the teacher's knowledge, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, to guide the student's training. Advanced methods have emerged, including multi-teacher distillation, self-distillation, and data-free approaches that work without the original training data. Knowledge distillation can also be combined with other compression methods like pruning and quantization to further enhance model efficiency, making powerful deep learning models accessible for resource-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Cross-modal Knowledge Distillation for Vision-to-Sensor Action Recognition
papers_seen.abstract: Human activity recognition (HAR) based on multi-modal approach has been recently shown to improve the accuracy performance of HAR. However, restricted computational resources associated with wearable devices, i.e., smartwatch, failed to directly support such advanced methods. To tackle this issue, this study introduces an end-to-end Vision-to-Sensor Knowledge Distillation (VSKD) framework. In this VSKD framework, only time-series data, i.e., accelerometer data, is needed from wearable devices during the testing phase. Therefore, this framework will not only reduce the computational demands on edge devices, but also produce a learning model that closely matches the performance of the computational expensive multi-modal approach. In order to retain the local temporal relationship and facilitate visual deep learning models, we first convert time-series data to two-dimensional images by applying the Gramian Angular Field ( GAF) based encoding method. We adopted ResNet18 and multi-scale TRN with BN-Inception as teacher and student network in this study, respectively. A novel loss function, named Distance and Angle-wised Semantic Knowledge loss (DASK), is proposed to mitigate the modality variations between the vision and the sensor domain. Extensive experimental results on UTD-MHAD, MMAct, and Berkeley-MHAD datasets demonstrate the effectiveness and competitiveness of the proposed VSKD model which can deployed on wearable sensors.

papers_seen.author: Moreno
papers_seen.title: Learning Perception-Aware Agile Flight in Cluttered Environments
papers_seen.abstract: Recently, neural control policies have outperformed existing model-based planning-and-control methods for autonomously navigating quadrotors through cluttered environments in minimum time. However, they are not perception aware, a crucial requirement in vision-based navigation due to the camera's limited field of view and the underactuated nature of a quadrotor. We propose a learning-based system that achieves perception-aware, agile flight in cluttered environments. Our method combines imitation learning with reinforcement learning (RL) by leveraging a privileged learning-by-cheating framework. Using RL, we first train a perception-aware teacher policy with full-state information to fly in minimum time through cluttered environments. Then, we use imitation learning to distill its knowledge into a vision-based student policy that only perceives the environment via a camera. Our approach tightly couples perception and control, showing a significant advantage in computation speed (10 times faster) and success rate. We demonstrate the closed-loop control performance using hardware-in-the-loop simulation.

papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Mason
papers_seen.title: Learning Student Networks via Feature Embedding
papers_seen.abstract: Deep convolutional neural networks have been widely used in numerous applications, but their demanding storage and computational resource requirements prevent their applications on mobile devices. Knowledge distillation aims to optimize a portable student network by taking the knowledge from a well-trained heavy teacher network. Traditional teacher-student based methods used to rely on additional fully-connected layers to bridge intermediate layers of teacher and student networks, which brings in a large number of auxiliary parameters. In contrast, this paper aims to propagate information from teacher to student without introducing new variables which need to be optimized. We regard the teacher-student paradigm from a new perspective of feature embedding. By introducing the locality preserving loss, the student network is encouraged to generate the low-dimensional features which could inherit intrinsic properties of their corresponding high-dimensional features from teacher network. The resulting portable network thus can naturally maintain the performance as that of the teacher network. Theoretical analysis is provided to justify the lower computation complexity of the proposed method. Experiments on benchmark datasets and well-trained networks suggest that the proposed algorithm is superior to state-of-the-art teacher-student learning methods in terms of computational and storage complexity.

This makes it a foundational strategy for developing practical, robust, and accessible artificial intelligence systems across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Wong
papers_seen.title: Embracing the Dark Knowledge: Domain Generalization Using Regularized Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Though convolutional neural networks are widely used in different tasks, lack of generalization capability in the absence of sufficient and representative data is one of the challenges that hinder their practical application. In this paper, we propose a simple, effective, and plug-and-play training strategy named Knowledge Distillation for Domain Generalization (KDDG) which is built upon a knowledge distillation framework with the gradient filter as a novel regularization term. We find that both the ``richer dark knowledge" from the teacher network, as well as the gradient filter we proposed, can reduce the difficulty of learning the mapping which further improves the generalization ability of the model. We also conduct experiments extensively to show that our framework can significantly improve the generalization capability of deep neural networks in different tasks including image classification, segmentation, reinforcement learning by comparing our method with existing state-of-the-art domain generalization techniques. Last but not the least, we propose to adopt two metrics to analyze our proposed method in order to better understand how our proposed method benefits the generalization capability of deep neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Oneill
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly reduced computational and memory costs. Initially developed for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used to improve model generalization, enhance robustness, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different domains, making it an indispensable tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Byrd
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning: A Framework for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for resource-constrained environments. The process involves a compact "student" model learning to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. The applications of this paradigm extend beyond simple compression, encompassing performance enhancement, improved model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility has established knowledge distillation as a fundamental tool in natural language processing, computer vision, and other domains.

papers_seen.author: Jordan
papers_seen.title: The Expanding Role of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning where knowledge from a large, complex "teacher" model is transferred to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Originally conceived as a method for model compression, its applications have expanded significantly. This technique not only enables the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments but also serves as a mechanism to enhance the performance of student models beyond what they could achieve through standard training. The versatility of knowledge distillation is demonstrated by its application across diverse domains, from natural language processing to computer vision. Recent advancements have introduced more dynamic and effective distillation frameworks, such as online and self-distillation, and have even leveraged the technique to improve model interpretability.

papers_seen.author: Gibson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, computationally expensive ones. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices such as mobile phones. While initially focused on reducing model size and latency, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded, making it a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer in complex learning scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Chavez
papers_seen.title: Data-Free Knowledge Distillation for Deep Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in model compression have provided procedures for compressing large neural networks to a fraction of their original size while retaining most if not all of their accuracy. However, all of these approaches rely on access to the original training set, which might not always be possible if the network to be compressed was trained on a very large dataset, or on a dataset whose release poses privacy or safety concerns as may be the case for biometrics tasks. We present a method for data-free knowledge distillation, which is able to compress deep neural networks trained on large-scale datasets to a fraction of their size leveraging only some extra metadata to be provided with a pretrained model release. We also explore different kinds of metadata that can be used with our method, and discuss tradeoffs involved in using each of them.

papers_seen.author: Everett
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm in deep learning that enables the creation of smaller, more efficient models from larger, more complex ones. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the performance of a larger teacher model. This process facilitates the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, where computational power and memory are limited. The applications of this technique are diverse, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond creating smaller and faster models, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve interpretability, and address challenges related to data privacy.

papers_seen.author: Graham
papers_seen.title: Multi-Level Branched Regularization for Federated Learning
papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.author: Henderson
papers_seen.title: Graph-less Neural Networks: Teaching Old MLPs New Tricks via Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) are popular for graph machine learning and have shown great results on wide node classification tasks. Yet, they are less popular for practical deployments in the industry owing to their scalability challenges incurred by data dependency. Namely, GNN inference depends on neighbor nodes multiple hops away from the target, and fetching them burdens latency-constrained applications. Existing inference acceleration methods like pruning and quantization can speed up GNNs by reducing Multiplication-and-ACcumulation (MAC) operations, but the improvements are limited given the data dependency is not resolved. Conversely, multi-layer perceptrons (MLPs) have no graph dependency and infer much faster than GNNs, even though they are less accurate than GNNs for node classification in general. Motivated by these complementary strengths and weaknesses, we bring GNNs and MLPs together via knowledge distillation (KD). Our work shows that the performance of MLPs can be improved by large margins with GNN KD. We call the distilled MLPs Graph-less Neural Networks (GLNNs) as they have no inference graph dependency. We show that GLNNs with competitive accuracy infer faster than GNNs by 146X-273X and faster than other acceleration methods by 14X-27X. Under a production setting involving both transductive and inductive predictions across 7 datasets, GLNN accuracies improve over stand-alone MLPs by 12.36% on average and match GNNs on 6/7 datasets. Comprehensive analysis shows when and why GLNNs can achieve competitive accuracies to GNNs and suggests GLNN as a handy choice for latency-constrained applications.

papers_seen.author: Larson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a popular technique in deep learning for model compression and knowledge transfer. The core idea involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process allows the student to learn from the rich representations and soft probability distributions generated by the teacher, often leading to significant performance improvements over training the student model from scratch. This method is applied across a wide range of domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a substantial loss in accuracy. Research in this area explores various distillation mechanisms, application-specific strategies, and the theoretical underpinnings of why and how this knowledge transfer is effective.

papers_seen.author: Lewis
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used in deep learning to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to emulate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, often through its output probabilities or internal representations, the student model can achieve high performance with significantly reduced computational and memory requirements. While initially developed for compression, the applications of this versatile framework have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Bowers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique that transfers knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, the 'student'. This process aims to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and requiring fewer computational resources. The fundamental idea is to train the student not only on the ground-truth labels but also on the soft probability distributions produced by the teacher model. This technique has been adapted in numerous ways, including transferring knowledge from intermediate layers, operating in data-free scenarios to preserve privacy, and even applying it across different tasks or data modalities. The ultimate goal is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy.

papers_seen.author: Morgan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. This process enables the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory requirements without a significant loss in performance. The applications of this technique are widespread, spanning natural language processing, where large language models are compressed into simpler networks, and computer vision for tasks like object detection. Modern approaches not only focus on the student's training but also explore methods for creating more effective teacher models. Knowledge distillation is often used in conjunction with other compression methods like pruning and quantization. Furthermore, the framework has been adapted to address contemporary challenges such as domain adaptation, data-free learning scenarios, and privacy preservation in federated learning environments.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.

papers_seen.author: Ruiz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the deployment challenges of large, computationally intensive models. It employs a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient "student" model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in accuracy. This versatile approach extends beyond simple size reduction, with applications in enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and facilitating knowledge transfer across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Fisher
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. This process involves a teacher-student framework where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, cumbersome teacher model. The primary objective is to enable the deployment of powerful deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments by reducing computational and memory demands without a substantial loss in performance. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple model compression. It has evolved into a versatile paradigm for addressing complex challenges such as domain adaptation, continual learning, and privacy preservation. By transferring knowledge in various forms, from output probabilities to intermediate feature representations, this framework enhances model efficiency, robustness, and adaptability across a wide range of applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Schultz
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly lower computational and memory costs. Beyond simple model size reduction, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework used to improve generalization, facilitate domain adaptation, and enable privacy-preserving collaborative learning, making it an indispensable tool for developing practical and accessible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Lawrence
papers_seen.title: Distilling Knowledge From a Deep Pose Regressor Network
papers_seen.abstract: This paper presents a novel method to distill knowledge from a deep pose regressor network for efficient Visual Odometry (VO). Standard distillation relies on "dark knowledge" for successful knowledge transfer. As this knowledge is not available in pose regression and the teacher prediction is not always accurate, we propose to emphasize the knowledge transfer only when we trust the teacher. We achieve this by using teacher loss as a confidence score which places variable relative importance on the teacher prediction. We inject this confidence score to the main training task via Attentive Imitation Loss (AIL) and when learning the intermediate representation of the teacher through Attentive Hint Training (AHT) approach. To the best of our knowledge, this is the first work which successfully distill the knowledge from a deep pose regression network. Our evaluation on the KITTI and Malaga dataset shows that we can keep the student prediction close to the teacher with up to 92.95% parameter reduction and 2.12x faster in computation time.

papers_seen.author: Benson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful paradigm in deep learning, primarily known as a model compression technique. It facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, pre-trained 'teacher' models. This process enables the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. However, the applications of this framework extend far beyond simple compression. Knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile tool for enhancing model performance, ensuring data privacy, and mitigating algorithmic and gender biases. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its critical role in developing practical, robust, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Hall
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Efficient and Versatile Deep Learning Models
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique for model compression and knowledge transfer in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to reduce computational and storage costs, making large models deployable on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This technique has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models, computer vision for optimizing generative networks, and reinforcement learning for policy transfer. Advanced methods have expanded upon the traditional framework, introducing data-free distillation, meta-learning approaches where the teacher adapts its teaching strategy, and multi-teacher setups. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has also been leveraged to enhance model interpretability and improve generalization across different data distributions, demonstrating its versatility as a powerful tool in the development of practical deep learning systems.

papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, especially in fields like natural language processing, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Model compression techniques aim to address this challenge by creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent and versatile framework for this purpose. This technique operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The goal is to produce a lightweight model that retains the high performance of its larger counterpart, making it suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including computer vision and natural language processing.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: White
papers_seen.title: Distilling portable Generative Adversarial Networks for Image Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning designed to compress large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. The process involves training a compact "student" model to mimic the behavior and outputs of a pre-trained, high-performance "teacher" model. This knowledge transfer enables the deployment of powerful artificial intelligence systems in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for model compression, the applications of distillation have expanded significantly, now serving as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling advanced learning paradigms like domain adaptation and federated learning.

papers_seen.author: Suarez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning for model compression, where a compact "student" model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, more complex "teacher" model. This process facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art neural networks in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, by significantly reducing their size and computational requirements. Beyond compression, knowledge distillation has evolved into a versatile framework capable of enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling novel applications across various domains. By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, student models can achieve higher accuracy and robustness than they could by training on ground-truth labels alone.

papers_seen.author: Bentley
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and flexible technique for model compression in deep learning. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones, without a significant loss in accuracy. While originally conceived for reducing model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now used not only for creating smaller and faster models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and addressing practical challenges like data privacy. This demonstrates its evolution from a simple compression tool into a multifaceted framework for developing more efficient, robust, and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Reed
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a fundamental model compression technique in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments. Through a teacher-student framework, a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers rich, generalized knowledge, enabling the creation of compact models with high performance. While its primary goal is to reduce model size and inference time, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It is now a versatile framework used to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and transfer knowledge across different architectures and data modalities, making it an indispensable tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks from larger, more complex ones. The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a pre-trained teacher model. This knowledge transfer enables the creation of lightweight models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile and edge devices, without a significant loss in performance. While its primary goal is size reduction, the applications of this versatile paradigm have expanded to include performance enhancement, robustness improvement, and enabling complex learning scenarios across various domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Sandoval
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has become a fundamental technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenges posed by the increasing size and complexity of modern neural networks. This method employs a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact, fast models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The versatility of this framework extends beyond simple compression, proving useful for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and facilitating knowledge transfer across different domains, making it a cornerstone of practical artificial intelligence development.

papers_seen.author: Short
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. By transferring the rich knowledge from the teacher, the student model can achieve comparable or even enhanced performance. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include improving model robustness, generalization, and facilitating advanced learning paradigms.

papers_seen.author: Brown
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation in Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning, primarily known for model compression. It enables the creation of smaller, more efficient 'student' models by transferring knowledge from larger, more complex 'teacher' models. This process is critical for deploying state-of-the-art networks in resource-constrained environments. However, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple compression. Its applications now encompass a wide range of objectives, including enhancing model interpretability, promoting algorithmic fairness, preserving data privacy in distributed learning settings, and unifying knowledge from multiple disparate models. While the process is not without its challenges, such as the potential for propagating teacher model errors, its flexibility across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision makes it a foundational and versatile tool for developing efficient, effective, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Horton
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile framework for model compression in deep learning. This technique operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This process makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on resource-constrained devices, such as mobile phones. The method's effectiveness has been demonstrated across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and reinforcement learning, making it a critical tool for developing practical and deployable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Holmes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, especially large pre-trained language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance but are often too large and computationally expensive for real-world applications. Model compression seeks to address this by creating smaller, more efficient models. Knowledge distillation is a popular compression technique where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the teacher's learned knowledge, enabling the student to achieve high accuracy with significantly fewer resources. Advanced distillation strategies include leveraging multiple teachers, transferring knowledge from intermediate model layers, and even operating in data-free scenarios where the original training set is unavailable. The versatility of knowledge distillation has led to its application in diverse areas beyond simple compression, including domain adaptation and mitigating model bias.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning to address the deployment challenges of large, computationally expensive models. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. Beyond simple model size reduction, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement, privacy preservation, and the transfer of specific model capabilities, establishing it as a versatile and powerful tool for optimizing and deploying state-of-the-art neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Anderson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Model Compression Technique in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression and training paradigm in which a compact 'student' model learns to mimic a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. The primary goal is to transfer the knowledge from the high-performing teacher to the student, enabling the creation of smaller, faster, and more efficient models that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. This knowledge transfer can occur in various forms, from mimicking the teacher's final output probabilities (soft labels) to replicating its intermediate feature representations. The technique has been successfully applied across numerous domains, including natural language processing for compressing large language models like BERT, and in computer vision for tasks such as object detection and image classification. Advanced distillation frameworks include using ensembles of teachers, adversarial training schemes, and self-distillation, where a model learns from its own past predictions. Furthermore, knowledge distillation is a key enabler for collaborative learning paradigms like federated learning, allowing knowledge transfer between heterogeneous devices.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression paradigm designed to create compact and efficient neural networks. This technique involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. By transferring knowledge from the cumbersome teacher to the lightweight student, this approach reduces computational and memory requirements, enabling the deployment of powerful deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, recommender systems, and graph-based learning, using a range of methods from mimicking output probabilities to distilling internal representations and employing adversarial learning frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Silva
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and Natural Language Processing
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, state-of-the-art deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The core principle is to transfer the nuanced knowledge learned by the teacher, often encapsulated in its soft predictions, to the more compact student network. This approach has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to compress models like large language transformers and generative adversarial networks. Advanced methods have been developed that utilize multiple teachers, distill knowledge from intermediate layers, and even operate in data-free settings to address privacy concerns. Furthermore, knowledge distillation plays a crucial role in communication-efficient frameworks like federated learning, demonstrating its versatility and importance in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Hurst
papers_seen.title: Ranking Distillation: Learning Compact Ranking Models With High Performance for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a novel way to train ranking models, such as recommender systems, that are both effective and efficient. Knowledge distillation (KD) was shown to be successful in image recognition to achieve both effectiveness and efficiency. We propose a KD technique for learning to rank problems, called \emph{ranking distillation (RD)}. Specifically, we train a smaller student model to learn to rank documents/items from both the training data and the supervision of a larger teacher model. The student model achieves a similar ranking performance to that of the large teacher model, but its smaller model size makes the online inference more efficient. RD is flexible because it is orthogonal to the choices of ranking models for the teacher and student. We address the challenges of RD for ranking problems. The experiments on public data sets and state-of-the-art recommendation models showed that RD achieves its design purposes: the student model learnt with RD has a model size less than half of the teacher model while achieving a ranking performance similar to the teacher model and much better than the student model learnt without RD.

papers_seen.author: Rodriguez
papers_seen.title: Extract the Knowledge of Graph Neural Networks and Go Beyond it: An Effective Knowledge Distillation Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Semi-supervised learning on graphs is an important problem in the machine learning area. In recent years, state-of-the-art classification methods based on graph neural networks (GNNs) have shown their superiority over traditional ones such as label propagation. However, the sophisticated architectures of these neural models will lead to a complex prediction mechanism, which could not make full use of valuable prior knowledge lying in the data, e.g., structurally correlated nodes tend to have the same class. In this paper, we propose a framework based on knowledge distillation to address the above issues. Our framework extracts the knowledge of an arbitrary learned GNN model (teacher model), and injects it into a well-designed student model. The student model is built with two simple prediction mechanisms, i.e., label propagation and feature transformation, which naturally preserves structure-based and feature-based prior knowledge, respectively. In specific, we design the student model as a trainable combination of parameterized label propagation and feature transformation modules. As a result, the learned student can benefit from both prior knowledge and the knowledge in GNN teachers for more effective predictions. Moreover, the learned student model has a more interpretable prediction process than GNNs. We conduct experiments on five public benchmark datasets and employ seven GNN models including GCN, GAT, APPNP, SAGE, SGC, GCNII and GLP as the teacher models. Experimental results show that the learned student model can consistently outperform its corresponding teacher model by 1.4% - 4.7% on average. Code and data are available at https://github.com/BUPT-GAMMA/CPF

papers_seen.author: Lynch
papers_seen.title: Revisiting Knowledge Distillation via Label Smoothing Regularization
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge Distillation (KD) aims to distill the knowledge of a cumbersome teacher model into a lightweight student model. Its success is generally attributed to the privileged information on similarities among categories provided by the teacher model, and in this sense, only strong teacher models are deployed to teach weaker students in practice. In this work, we challenge this common belief by following experimental observations: 1) beyond the acknowledgment that the teacher can improve the student, the student can also enhance the teacher significantly by reversing the KD procedure; 2) a poorly-trained teacher with much lower accuracy than the student can still improve the latter significantly. To explain these observations, we provide a theoretical analysis of the relationships between KD and label smoothing regularization. We prove that 1) KD is a type of learned label smoothing regularization and 2) label smoothing regularization provides a virtual teacher model for KD. From these results, we argue that the success of KD is not fully due to the similarity information between categories from teachers, but also to the regularization of soft targets, which is equally or even more important.   Based on these analyses, we further propose a novel Teacher-free Knowledge Distillation (Tf-KD) framework, where a student model learns from itself or manuallydesigned regularization distribution. The Tf-KD achieves comparable performance with normal KD from a superior teacher, which is well applied when a stronger teacher model is unavailable. Meanwhile, Tf-KD is generic and can be directly deployed for training deep neural networks. Without any extra computation cost, Tf-KD achieves up to 0.65\% improvement on ImageNet over well-established baseline models, which is superior to label smoothing regularization.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create smaller, more computationally efficient models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student to replicate the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its broad application and its evolution into more advanced methods, including data-free distillation and self-distillation, which extend its utility beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and improved generalization.

papers_seen.author: Doyle
papers_seen.title: DE-RRD: A Knowledge Distillation Framework for Recommender System
papers_seen.abstract: Recent recommender systems have started to employ knowledge distillation, which is a model compression technique distilling knowledge from a cumbersome model (teacher) to a compact model (student), to reduce inference latency while maintaining performance. The state-of-the-art methods have only focused on making the student model accurately imitate the predictions of the teacher model. They have a limitation in that the prediction results incompletely reveal the teacher's knowledge. In this paper, we propose a novel knowledge distillation framework for recommender system, called DE-RRD, which enables the student model to learn from the latent knowledge encoded in the teacher model as well as from the teacher's predictions. Concretely, DE-RRD consists of two methods: 1) Distillation Experts (DE) that directly transfers the latent knowledge from the teacher model. DE exploits "experts" and a novel expert selection strategy for effectively distilling the vast teacher's knowledge to the student with limited capacity. 2) Relaxed Ranking Distillation (RRD) that transfers the knowledge revealed from the teacher's prediction with consideration of the relaxed ranking orders among items. Our extensive experiments show that DE-RRD outperforms the state-of-the-art competitors and achieves comparable or even better performance to that of the teacher model with faster inference time.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.author: Miller
papers_seen.title: Understanding BERT Rankers Under Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep language models such as BERT pre-trained on large corpus have given a huge performance boost to the state-of-the-art information retrieval ranking systems. Knowledge embedded in such models allows them to pick up complex matching signals between passages and queries. However, the high computation cost during inference limits their deployment in real-world search scenarios. In this paper, we study if and how the knowledge for search within BERT can be transferred to a smaller ranker through distillation. Our experiments demonstrate that it is crucial to use a proper distillation procedure, which produces up to nine times speedup while preserving the state-of-the-art performance.

papers_seen.author: Liu
papers_seen.title: Enabling Multimodal Generation on CLIP via Vision-Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The recent large-scale vision-language pre-training (VLP) of dual-stream architectures (e.g., CLIP) with a tremendous amount of image-text pair data, has shown its superiority on various multimodal alignment tasks. Despite its success, the resulting models are not capable of multimodal generative tasks due to the weak text encoder. To tackle this problem, we propose to augment the dual-stream VLP model with a textual pre-trained language model (PLM) via vision-language knowledge distillation (VLKD), enabling the capability for multimodal generation. VLKD is pretty data- and computation-efficient compared to the pre-training from scratch. Experimental results show that the resulting model has strong zero-shot performance on multimodal generation tasks, such as open-ended visual question answering and image captioning. For example, it achieves 44.5% zero-shot accuracy on the VQAv2 dataset, surpassing the previous state-of-the-art zero-shot model with $7\times$ fewer parameters. Furthermore, the original textual language understanding and generation ability of the PLM is maintained after VLKD, which makes our model versatile for both multimodal and unimodal tasks.

papers_seen.title: Distilling the Knowledge of BERT for Sequence-to-Sequence ASR
papers_seen.abstract: Attention-based sequence-to-sequence (seq2seq) models have achieved promising results in automatic speech recognition (ASR). However, as these models decode in a left-to-right way, they do not have access to context on the right. We leverage both left and right context by applying BERT as an external language model to seq2seq ASR through knowledge distillation. In our proposed method, BERT generates soft labels to guide the training of seq2seq ASR. Furthermore, we leverage context beyond the current utterance as input to BERT. Experimental evaluations show that our method significantly improves the ASR performance from the seq2seq baseline on the Corpus of Spontaneous Japanese (CSJ). Knowledge distillation from BERT outperforms that from a transformer LM that only looks at left context. We also show the effectiveness of leveraging context beyond the current utterance. Our method outperforms other LM application approaches such as n-best rescoring and shallow fusion, while it does not require extra inference cost.

papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models, particularly large-scale language models, have achieved state-of-the-art performance across numerous tasks. However, their immense size and computational requirements pose significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, especially knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution to this problem. This paper argues that knowledge distillation is a highly effective and versatile framework for compressing deep learning models, enabling their practical application in diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems. papers_seen.author: Wood
papers_seen.title: What Makes a "Good" Data Augmentation in Knowledge Distillation -- A Statistical Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation (KD) is a general neural network training approach that uses a teacher model to guide the student model. Existing works mainly study KD from the network output side (e.g., trying to design a better KD loss function), while few have attempted to understand it from the input side. Especially, its interplay with data augmentation (DA) has not been well understood. In this paper, we ask: Why do some DA schemes (e.g., CutMix) inherently perform much better than others in KD? What makes a "good" DA in KD? Our investigation from a statistical perspective suggests that a good DA scheme should reduce the covariance of the teacher-student cross-entropy. A practical metric, the stddev of teacher's mean probability (T. stddev), is further presented and well justified empirically. Besides the theoretical understanding, we also introduce a new entropy-based data-mixing DA scheme, CutMixPick, to further enhance CutMix. Extensive empirical studies support our claims and demonstrate how we can harvest considerable performance gains simply by using a better DA scheme in knowledge distillation.

papers_seen.author: Robertson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning that operates on a teacher-student paradigm. It addresses the challenge of deploying large, complex models in resource-constrained environments by training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher by having the student replicate the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. While the primary goal is to create lightweight models with minimal performance loss, the technique also serves to enhance model performance and generalization. The framework has evolved to include advanced methods like multi-teacher and data-free distillation, with widespread applications in fields such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Jones

This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Schultz

papers_seen.author: Haynes
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning models, while powerful, are often too large and computationally expensive for practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to overcome this limitation. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher to the student, enabling the creation of compact models that maintain high performance with significantly reduced computational and memory requirements. This versatile framework facilitates the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments and has expanded to applications beyond compression, including performance enhancement and improving model fairness.

papers_seen.author: Fowler
papers_seen.title: SEED: Self-supervised Distillation For Visual Representation
papers_seen.abstract: This paper is concerned with self-supervised learning for small models. The problem is motivated by our empirical studies that while the widely used contrastive self-supervised learning method has shown great progress on large model training, it does not work well for small models. To address this problem, we propose a new learning paradigm, named SElf-SupErvised Distillation (SEED), where we leverage a larger network (as Teacher) to transfer its representational knowledge into a smaller architecture (as Student) in a self-supervised fashion. Instead of directly learning from unlabeled data, we train a student encoder to mimic the similarity score distribution inferred by a teacher over a set of instances. We show that SEED dramatically boosts the performance of small networks on downstream tasks. Compared with self-supervised baselines, SEED improves the top-1 accuracy from 42.2% to 67.6% on EfficientNet-B0 and from 36.3% to 68.2% on MobileNet-v3-Large on the ImageNet-1k dataset.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: AutoGAN-Distiller: Searching to Compress Generative Adversarial Networks
papers_seen.abstract: The compression of Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) has lately drawn attention, due to the increasing demand for deploying GANs into mobile devices for numerous applications such as image translation, enhancement and editing. However, compared to the substantial efforts to compressing other deep models, the research on compressing GANs (usually the generators) remains at its infancy stage. Existing GAN compression algorithms are limited to handling specific GAN architectures and losses. Inspired by the recent success of AutoML in deep compression, we introduce AutoML to GAN compression and develop an AutoGAN-Distiller (AGD) framework. Starting with a specifically designed efficient search space, AGD performs an end-to-end discovery for new efficient generators, given the target computational resource constraints. The search is guided by the original GAN model via knowledge distillation, therefore fulfilling the compression. AGD is fully automatic, standalone (i.e., needing no trained discriminators), and generically applicable to various GAN models. We evaluate AGD in two representative GAN tasks: image translation and super resolution. Without bells and whistles, AGD yields remarkably lightweight yet more competitive compressed models, that largely outperform existing alternatives. Our codes and pretrained models are available at https://github.com/TAMU-VITA/AGD.

papers_seen.title: Moonshine: Distilling with Cheap Convolutions
papers_seen.abstract: Many engineers wish to deploy modern neural networks in memory-limited settings; but the development of flexible methods for reducing memory use is in its infancy, and there is little knowledge of the resulting cost-benefit. We propose structural model distillation for memory reduction using a strategy that produces a student architecture that is a simple transformation of the teacher architecture: no redesign is needed, and the same hyperparameters can be used. Using attention transfer, we provide Pareto curves/tables for distillation of residual networks with four benchmark datasets, indicating the memory versus accuracy payoff. We show that substantial memory savings are possible with very little loss of accuracy, and confirm that distillation provides student network performance that is better than training that student architecture directly on data.
