papers_seen.author: Adams
papers_seen.title: A Closer Look at Deep Learning Heuristics: Learning rate restarts, Warmup and Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: The convergence rate and final performance of common deep learning models have significantly benefited from heuristics such as learning rate schedules, knowledge distillation, skip connections, and normalization layers. In the absence of theoretical underpinnings, controlled experiments aimed at explaining these strategies can aid our understanding of deep learning landscapes and the training dynamics. Existing approaches for empirical analysis rely on tools of linear interpolation and visualizations with dimensionality reduction, each with their limitations. Instead, we revisit such analysis of heuristics through the lens of recently proposed methods for loss surface and representation analysis, viz., mode connectivity and canonical correlation analysis (CCA), and hypothesize reasons for the success of the heuristics. In particular, we explore knowledge distillation and learning rate heuristics of (cosine) restarts and warmup using mode connectivity and CCA. Our empirical analysis suggests that: (a) the reasons often quoted for the success of cosine annealing are not evidenced in practice; (b) that the effect of learning rate warmup is to prevent the deeper layers from creating training instability; and (c) that the latent knowledge shared by the teacher is primarily disbursed to the deeper layers.

papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Rice
papers_seen.title: CoReD: Generalizing Fake Media Detection with Continual Representation using Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Over the last few decades, artificial intelligence research has made tremendous strides, but it still heavily relies on fixed datasets in stationary environments. Continual learning is a growing field of research that examines how AI systems can learn sequentially from a continuous stream of linked data in the same way that biological systems do. Simultaneously, fake media such as deepfakes and synthetic face images have emerged as significant to current multimedia technologies. Recently, numerous method has been proposed which can detect deepfakes with high accuracy. However, they suffer significantly due to their reliance on fixed datasets in limited evaluation settings. Therefore, in this work, we apply continuous learning to neural networks' learning dynamics, emphasizing its potential to increase data efficiency significantly. We propose Continual Representation using Distillation (CoReD) method that employs the concept of Continual Learning (CL), Representation Learning (RL), and Knowledge Distillation (KD). We design CoReD to perform sequential domain adaptation tasks on new deepfake and GAN-generated synthetic face datasets, while effectively minimizing the catastrophic forgetting in a teacher-student model setting. Our extensive experimental results demonstrate that our method is efficient at domain adaptation to detect low-quality deepfakes videos and GAN-generated images from several datasets, outperforming the-state-of-art baseline methods.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenges of deploying large, computationally intensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to create compact, fast models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a substantial loss in performance. By transferring the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, the student can achieve high accuracy. The applications of knowledge distillation have expanded beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer across different domains, and improving model robustness, making it a foundational tool for developing practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Conner
papers_seen.title: Distilling Task-Specific Knowledge from BERT into Simple Neural Networks
papers_seen.abstract: In the natural language processing literature, neural networks are becoming increasingly deeper and complex. The recent poster child of this trend is the deep language representation model, which includes BERT, ELMo, and GPT. These developments have led to the conviction that previous-generation, shallower neural networks for language understanding are obsolete. In this paper, however, we demonstrate that rudimentary, lightweight neural networks can still be made competitive without architecture changes, external training data, or additional input features. We propose to distill knowledge from BERT, a state-of-the-art language representation model, into a single-layer BiLSTM, as well as its siamese counterpart for sentence-pair tasks. Across multiple datasets in paraphrasing, natural language inference, and sentiment classification, we achieve comparable results with ELMo, while using roughly 100 times fewer parameters and 15 times less inference time.

papers_seen.author: Calderon
papers_seen.title: Learning Generalizable Models for Vehicle Routing Problems via Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.author: Cannon
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process typically involves a teacher-student framework, where a smaller student model learns to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This paradigm addresses the significant computational and storage costs associated with state-of-the-art models in fields like Natural Language Processing and computer vision. Various methods have been developed to tackle challenges such as data privacy, architectural mismatches between teacher and student, and information transfer efficiency. Applications are diverse, ranging from compressing large language models and generative adversarial networks to enhancing model robustness against adversarial attacks and enabling efficient federated learning. Extensions to the basic framework include using multiple teachers, adversarial learning, and data-free distillation techniques, continually expanding the utility of this compression strategy.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Reinforced Multi-Teacher Selection for Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: In natural language processing (NLP) tasks, slow inference speed and huge footprints in GPU usage remain the bottleneck of applying pre-trained deep models in production. As a popular method for model compression, knowledge distillation transfers knowledge from one or multiple large (teacher) models to a small (student) model. When multiple teacher models are available in distillation, the state-of-the-art methods assign a fixed weight to a teacher model in the whole distillation. Furthermore, most of the existing methods allocate an equal weight to every teacher model. In this paper, we observe that, due to the complexity of training examples and the differences in student model capability, learning differentially from teacher models can lead to better performance of student models distilled. We systematically develop a reinforced method to dynamically assign weights to teacher models for different training instances and optimize the performance of student model. Our extensive experimental results on several NLP tasks clearly verify the feasibility and effectiveness of our approach.

The primary goal is to create compact, fast models suitable for resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices, without a significant loss in performance. The applications of this framework are widespread, spanning natural language processing and computer vision. Beyond simple size reduction, knowledge distillation is also used to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and facilitate knowledge transfer across different tasks and modalities.

papers_seen.author: Humphrey
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Paradigm for Model Compression and Knowledge Transfer
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. Originally conceived as a method for a smaller "student" model to learn from a larger "teacher" model, the paradigm has evolved significantly. Research now shows that the benefits of distillation extend beyond simple mimicry, with the regularization effects of soft labels playing a crucial role. This technique has proven effective in a wide array of complex domains, including natural language processing for text generation and translation, the compression of generative adversarial networks, and the optimization of graph neural networks. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, adversarial training, and extensions for domain adaptation further highlight its versatility. Ultimately, knowledge distillation is a critical tool for creating efficient, yet powerful, AI systems suitable for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Farrell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Deep learning has produced increasingly large and complex models that achieve state-of-the-art performance but are often impractical for deployment due to their computational and memory requirements. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, address this challenge by transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. This process enables the creation of compact models that retain a significant portion of the teacher's performance, making them suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. The flexibility of knowledge distillation is evident in its successful application across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and graph-based learning, as well as its adaptability to scenarios where the original training data is unavailable.

papers_seen.abstract: In recent years, the fields of natural language processing (NLP) and information retrieval (IR) have made tremendous progress thanksto deep learning models like Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), Gated Recurrent Units (GRUs) and Long Short-Term Memory (LSTMs)networks, and Transformer [120] based models like Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (BERT) [24], GenerativePre-training Transformer (GPT-2) [94], Multi-task Deep Neural Network (MT-DNN) [73], Extra-Long Network (XLNet) [134], Text-to-text transfer transformer (T5) [95], T-NLG [98] and GShard [63]. papers_seen.author: Dean
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework Beyond Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is widely recognized as a powerful model compression technique in deep learning, designed to create smaller, more efficient models from larger, cumbersome ones. This process involves a 'teacher-student' framework where a compact student model learns to mimic the rich outputs of a pre-trained teacher. While its primary application is to enable the deployment of state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, the utility of knowledge distillation extends far beyond simple size reduction. It has evolved into a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness against adversarial attacks, and increasing model interpretability. Furthermore, advanced distillation methods can facilitate knowledge transfer in challenging scenarios, such as when the original training data is unavailable. This multifaceted capability establishes knowledge distillation not just as a compression tool, but as a fundamental paradigm for developing more practical, adaptable, and robust artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Bishop
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient neural networks from larger, more complex ones. The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and replicate the knowledge of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to reduce the computational and memory footprint of state-of-the-art models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. This knowledge transfer allows the student model to achieve high performance, often superior to what it could attain if trained on data alone. The technique's applications have expanded beyond simple compression into a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios across domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

By transferring the rich, nuanced knowledge from the teacher, including its predictions on unlabeled data, the student model can achieve comparable performance to its larger counterpart while being significantly smaller and faster. This technique has proven effective across a wide range of applications, from compressing large language models to enabling efficient object detection and transferring knowledge across different data modalities, making it a critical tool for creating practical, real-world artificial intelligence systems.

The process involves a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge embedded in the teacher's predictions or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters. Advanced methods such as self-distillation, online distillation, and data-free approaches further increase its versatility, making it a critical tool for developing efficient and practical AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Mayo
papers_seen.title: Rethinking Soft Labels for Knowledge Distillation: A Bias-Variance Tradeoff Perspective
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective approach to leverage a well-trained network or an ensemble of them, named as the teacher, to guide the training of a student network. The outputs from the teacher network are used as soft labels for supervising the training of a new network. Recent studies \citep{muller2019does,yuan2020revisiting} revealed an intriguing property of the soft labels that making labels soft serves as a good regularization to the student network. From the perspective of statistical learning, regularization aims to reduce the variance, however how bias and variance change is not clear for training with soft labels. In this paper, we investigate the bias-variance tradeoff brought by distillation with soft labels. Specifically, we observe that during training the bias-variance tradeoff varies sample-wisely. Further, under the same distillation temperature setting, we observe that the distillation performance is negatively associated with the number of some specific samples, which are named as regularization samples since these samples lead to bias increasing and variance decreasing. Nevertheless, we empirically find that completely filtering out regularization samples also deteriorates distillation performance. Our discoveries inspired us to propose the novel weighted soft labels to help the network adaptively handle the sample-wise bias-variance tradeoff. Experiments on standard evaluation benchmarks validate the effectiveness of our method. Our code is available at \url{https://github.com/bellymonster/Weighted-Soft-Label-Distillation}.

This approach has proven effective across a wide range of applications, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, demonstrating its versatility in making advanced AI more accessible and practical.

The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending to compressing large language models, improving low-precision networks, and enabling collaborative training in privacy-sensitive settings like federated learning. Furthermore, research challenges the conventional view of a superior teacher guiding a weaker student, suggesting that the regularization effect of the process is a key component of its success, even leading to teacher-free distillation frameworks.

papers_seen.author: Davis
papers_seen.title: Feature-map-level Online Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Feature maps contain rich information about image intensity and spatial correlation. However, previous online knowledge distillation methods only utilize the class probabilities. Thus in this paper, we propose an online knowledge distillation method that transfers not only the knowledge of the class probabilities but also that of the feature map using the adversarial training framework. We train multiple networks simultaneously by employing discriminators to distinguish the feature map distributions of different networks. Each network has its corresponding discriminator which discriminates the feature map from its own as fake while classifying that of the other network as real. By training a network to fool the corresponding discriminator, it can learn the other network's feature map distribution. We show that our method performs better than the conventional direct alignment method such as L1 and is more suitable for online distillation. Also, we propose a novel cyclic learning scheme for training more than two networks together. We have applied our method to various network architectures on the classification task and discovered a significant improvement of performance especially in the case of training a pair of a small network and a large one.

papers_seen.author: Le
papers_seen.title: VPN++: Rethinking Video-Pose embeddings for understanding Activities of Daily Living
papers_seen.abstract: Many attempts have been made towards combining RGB and 3D poses for the recognition of Activities of Daily Living (ADL). ADL may look very similar and often necessitate to model fine-grained details to distinguish them. Because the recent 3D ConvNets are too rigid to capture the subtle visual patterns across an action, this research direction is dominated by methods combining RGB and 3D Poses. But the cost of computing 3D poses from RGB stream is high in the absence of appropriate sensors. This limits the usage of aforementioned approaches in real-world applications requiring low latency. Then, how to best take advantage of 3D Poses for recognizing ADL? To this end, we propose an extension of a pose driven attention mechanism: Video-Pose Network (VPN), exploring two distinct directions. One is to transfer the Pose knowledge into RGB through a feature-level distillation and the other towards mimicking pose driven attention through an attention-level distillation. Finally, these two approaches are integrated into a single model, we call VPN++. We show that VPN++ is not only effective but also provides a high speed up and high resilience to noisy Poses. VPN++, with or without 3D Poses, outperforms the representative baselines on 4 public datasets. Code is available at https://github.com/srijandas07/vpnplusplus.

papers_seen.title: R2L: Distilling Neural Radiance Field to Neural Light Field for Efficient Novel View Synthesis
papers_seen.abstract: Recent research explosion on Neural Radiance Field (NeRF) shows the encouraging potential to represent complex scenes with neural networks. One major drawback of NeRF is its prohibitive inference time: Rendering a single pixel requires querying the NeRF network hundreds of times. To resolve it, existing efforts mainly attempt to reduce the number of required sampled points. However, the problem of iterative sampling still exists. On the other hand, Neural Light Field (NeLF) presents a more straightforward representation over NeRF in novel view synthesis -- the rendering of a pixel amounts to one single forward pass without ray-marching. In this work, we present a deep residual MLP network (88 layers) to effectively learn the light field. We show the key to successfully learning such a deep NeLF network is to have sufficient data, for which we transfer the knowledge from a pre-trained NeRF model via data distillation. Extensive experiments on both synthetic and real-world scenes show the merits of our method over other counterpart algorithms. On the synthetic scenes, we achieve 26-35x FLOPs reduction (per camera ray) and 28-31x runtime speedup, meanwhile delivering significantly better (1.4-2.8 dB average PSNR improvement) rendering quality than NeRF without any customized parallelism requirement.

papers_seen.title: Zero-shot Knowledge Transfer via Adversarial Belief Matching
papers_seen.abstract: Performing knowledge transfer from a large teacher network to a smaller student is a popular task in modern deep learning applications. However, due to growing dataset sizes and stricter privacy regulations, it is increasingly common not to have access to the data that was used to train the teacher. We propose a novel method which trains a student to match the predictions of its teacher without using any data or metadata. We achieve this by training an adversarial generator to search for images on which the student poorly matches the teacher, and then using them to train the student. Our resulting student closely approximates its teacher for simple datasets like SVHN, and on CIFAR10 we improve on the state-of-the-art for few-shot distillation (with 100 images per class), despite using no data. Finally, we also propose a metric to quantify the degree of belief matching between teacher and student in the vicinity of decision boundaries, and observe a significantly higher match between our zero-shot student and the teacher, than between a student distilled with real data and the teacher. Code available at: https://github.com/polo5/ZeroShotKnowledgeTransfer

The process operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to significantly reduce the computational and memory requirements of state-of-the-art models, enabling their deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile and edge devices. This method transfers the rich, generalized knowledge captured by the teacher, allowing the student to achieve high performance. While initially developed for compression, the applications of this versatile framework have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer across diverse domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Galvan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Model Compression Technique
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in real-world applications, particularly in resource-constrained environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful and versatile model compression technique to address this issue. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, this process enables the creation of compact, high-performance models that are suitable for devices with limited computational power or strict latency requirements. The applications of this technique are broad, spanning natural language processing, computer vision, and beyond, making it a critical tool for operationalizing state-of-the-art artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Gardner
papers_seen.title: Adversarially Robust Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is effective for producing small, high-performance neural networks for classification, but these small networks are vulnerable to adversarial attacks. This paper studies how adversarial robustness transfers from teacher to student during knowledge distillation. We find that a large amount of robustness may be inherited by the student even when distilled on only clean images. Second, we introduce Adversarially Robust Distillation (ARD) for distilling robustness onto student networks. In addition to producing small models with high test accuracy like conventional distillation, ARD also passes the superior robustness of large networks onto the student. In our experiments, we find that ARD student models decisively outperform adversarially trained networks of identical architecture in terms of robust accuracy, surpassing state-of-the-art methods on standard robustness benchmarks. Finally, we adapt recent fast adversarial training methods to ARD for accelerated robust distillation.

papers_seen.author: Oconnell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller footprint and faster inference speed. While its primary goal is to create compact and efficient models, the applications of this framework have expanded significantly, serving to enhance model performance, improve robustness, and enable knowledge transfer in specialized domains like natural language processing and graph neural networks.

papers_seen.author: Hahn
papers_seen.title: PKD: General Distillation Framework for Object Detectors via Pearson Correlation Coefficient
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation(KD) is a widely-used technique to train compact models in object detection. However, there is still a lack of study on how to distill between heterogeneous detectors. In this paper, we empirically find that better FPN features from a heterogeneous teacher detector can help the student although their detection heads and label assignments are different. However, directly aligning the feature maps to distill detectors suffers from two problems. First, the difference in feature magnitude between the teacher and the student could enforce overly strict constraints on the student. Second, the FPN stages and channels with large feature magnitude from the teacher model could dominate the gradient of distillation loss, which will overwhelm the effects of other features in KD and introduce much noise. To address the above issues, we propose to imitate features with Pearson Correlation Coefficient to focus on the relational information from the teacher and relax constraints on the magnitude of the features. Our method consistently outperforms the existing detection KD methods and works for both homogeneous and heterogeneous student-teacher pairs. Furthermore, it converges faster. With a powerful MaskRCNN-Swin detector as the teacher, ResNet-50 based RetinaNet and FCOS achieve 41.5% and 43.9% mAP on COCO2017, which are 4.1\% and 4.8\% higher than the baseline, respectively.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression

It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. papers_seen.author: Daniels
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: An Effective and Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial and highly effective technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. The process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This transfer of knowledge allows for the creation of compact models that retain high performance while being suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices. The applications of this paradigm have expanded significantly beyond simple size reduction, now encompassing tasks like performance enhancement, improving model robustness, and enabling learning in privacy-sensitive settings. This versatility establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational framework for developing practical, deployable, and powerful artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Jones
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Performance Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique for model compression, enabling the creation of smaller, more efficient student models by transferring knowledge from larger, cumbersome teacher models. This process allows for the deployment of state-of-the-art deep learning architectures in resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple compression, knowledge distillation has emerged as a versatile framework that can also enhance a model's generalization capabilities, improve its robustness against adversarial attacks, and increase its interpretability. By leveraging the rich information contained in a teacher's predictions, this technique offers a multifaceted approach to optimizing neural networks for a wide range of practical applications in natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Lin
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: From Model Compression to a Versatile Deep Learning Framework
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent technique in deep learning, initially developed for model compression. It enables the creation of small, efficient "student" models by transferring knowledge from large, complex "teacher" models, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. While its primary use is to reduce computational and memory footprints, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. It has evolved into a versatile framework used not only for creating compact models but also for enhancing model performance, improving interpretability, and enabling novel forms of knowledge transfer across different domains, modalities, and architectures. This demonstrates its crucial role in developing more practical, robust, and capable artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Evans
papers_seen.title: Learning Compact Metrics for MT
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in machine translation and multilingual text generation have led researchers to adopt trained metrics such as COMET or BLEURT, which treat evaluation as a regression problem and use representations from multilingual pre-trained models such as XLM-RoBERTa or mBERT. Yet studies on related tasks suggest that these models are most efficient when they are large, which is costly and impractical for evaluation. We investigate the trade-off between multilinguality and model capacity with RemBERT, a state-of-the-art multilingual language model, using data from the WMT Metrics Shared Task. We present a series of experiments which show that model size is indeed a bottleneck for cross-lingual transfer, then demonstrate how distillation can help addressing this bottleneck, by leveraging synthetic data generation and transferring knowledge from one teacher to multiple students trained on related languages. Our method yields up to 10.5% improvement over vanilla fine-tuning and reaches 92.6% of RemBERT's performance using only a third of its parameters.

papers_seen.author: Leblanc
papers_seen.title: The Versatility of Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of state-of-the-art deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment in resource-constrained environments. Model compression techniques, particularly knowledge distillation, have emerged as a powerful solution. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient 'student' model to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. Knowledge distillation has proven to be a highly versatile and effective method, extending far beyond simple model size reduction for classification tasks. Its applications span diverse domains such as natural language processing, computer vision, and graph-based learning. The framework is adaptable, enabling knowledge transfer between models of different architectures, across different data modalities, and even in scenarios with limited or no access to the original training data. This demonstrates its crucial role in making advanced AI models more practical and accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.author: Mcmillan
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. This process transfers the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. Beyond simple compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model robustness, facilitating training without original data, and improving overall performance. Its adaptability across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, highlights its role as a foundational tool for creating practical and efficient AI systems.

This process facilitates the deployment of powerful, state-of-the-art models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. While initially conceived for creating smaller and faster models, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling knowledge transfer in privacy-sensitive scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Campbell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model learns from a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process enables the deployment of powerful but cumbersome neural networks in resource-constrained environments by significantly reducing their size and computational cost. While its initial purpose was compression, the utility of knowledge distillation has expanded considerably. It now serves as a versatile framework for enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and enabling knowledge transfer in specialized and privacy-sensitive scenarios. Its adaptability across domains like natural language processing, computer vision, and federated learning demonstrates its indispensable role in creating practical and efficient artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Parsons
papers_seen.title: Curriculum Learning for Dense Retrieval Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Recent work has shown that more effective dense retrieval models can be obtained by distilling ranking knowledge from an existing base re-ranking model. In this paper, we propose a generic curriculum learning based optimization framework called CL-DRD that controls the difficulty level of training data produced by the re-ranking (teacher) model. CL-DRD iteratively optimizes the dense retrieval (student) model by increasing the difficulty of the knowledge distillation data made available to it. In more detail, we initially provide the student model coarse-grained preference pairs between documents in the teacher's ranking and progressively move towards finer-grained pairwise document ordering requirements. In our experiments, we apply a simple implementation of the CL-DRD framework to enhance two state-of-the-art dense retrieval models. Experiments on three public passage retrieval datasets demonstrate the effectiveness of our proposed framework.

papers_seen.author: Allen
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Versatile Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is an effective model compression technique that facilitates the deployment of large, complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments. This process involves training a smaller, more efficient "student" model to replicate the behavior of a larger, pre-trained "teacher" model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including its understanding of data structure and inter-class relationships, the student model can achieve performance far superior to what it could by training on the data alone. This approach has proven successful across various domains, including natural language processing, speech recognition, and computer vision, enabling the creation of compact models that are faster and require less memory without a significant drop in accuracy. The flexibility of knowledge distillation allows it to be combined with other techniques like data augmentation and federated learning, extending its applicability to diverse and challenging scenarios such as privacy-preservation and few-shot learning.

papers_seen.author: Edwards
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of modern deep learning models present significant challenges for deployment on resource-constrained devices. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key model compression technique to address this issue. Operating on a teacher-student paradigm, this method trains a smaller, more efficient student model to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to create compact and fast models that retain high accuracy, making them suitable for real-world applications. Beyond simple size reduction, the versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its successful application in enhancing model performance, improving generalization, and transferring knowledge across diverse domains.

papers_seen.author: Wilson
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression and Enhancement in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique in deep learning and natural language processing. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create compact, high-performance models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments, such as mobile devices. This process allows for a significant reduction in model size and inference time while retaining the capabilities of the larger counterpart. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, knowledge transfer in privacy-preserving scenarios like federated learning, and improving model robustness across various domains.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile framework for model compression in deep learning. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by operating on a teacher-student paradigm. A smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models that retain high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. Its success across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, has established it as a foundational tool for developing efficient and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Cameron
papers_seen.title: Well-Read Students Learn Better: On the Importance of Pre-training Compact Models
papers_seen.abstract: Recent developments in natural language representations have been accompanied by large and expensive models that leverage vast amounts of general-domain text through self-supervised pre-training. Due to the cost of applying such models to down-stream tasks, several model compression techniques on pre-trained language representations have been proposed (Sun et al., 2019; Sanh, 2019). However, surprisingly, the simple baseline of just pre-training and fine-tuning compact models has been overlooked. In this paper, we first show that pre-training remains important in the context of smaller architectures, and fine-tuning pre-trained compact models can be competitive to more elaborate methods proposed in concurrent work. Starting with pre-trained compact models, we then explore transferring task knowledge from large fine-tuned models through standard knowledge distillation. The resulting simple, yet effective and general algorithm, Pre-trained Distillation, brings further improvements. Through extensive experiments, we more generally explore the interaction between pre-training and distillation under two variables that have been under-studied: model size and properties of unlabeled task data. One surprising observation is that they have a compound effect even when sequentially applied on the same data. To accelerate future research, we will make our 24 pre-trained miniature BERT models publicly available.

papers_seen.author: Stevens
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning designed to create smaller, more efficient models suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments. This process involves a teacher-student framework, where a compact 'student' model is trained to replicate the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The student learns from the rich, nuanced information provided by the teacher, such as its output probabilities or internal feature representations. This allows for the development of lightweight yet powerful models across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, without a significant loss in performance.

papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning that facilitates the creation of smaller, more efficient models by transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained model to a more compact one. This teacher-student paradigm is primarily used for model compression, enabling the deployment of state-of-the-art architectures on resource-constrained devices. However, its utility extends significantly beyond this initial purpose. The method has been successfully adapted to enhance model performance, improve generalization, and address critical concerns such as data privacy, algorithmic fairness, and model interpretability. Its flexibility across diverse domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, establishes knowledge distillation as a foundational tool for developing practical, efficient, and responsible artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Abbott
papers_seen.title: Compressing Deep Graph Neural Networks via Adversarial Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Deep graph neural networks (GNNs) have been shown to be expressive for modeling graph-structured data. Nevertheless, the over-stacked architecture of deep graph models makes it difficult to deploy and rapidly test on mobile or embedded systems. To compress over-stacked GNNs, knowledge distillation via a teacher-student architecture turns out to be an effective technique, where the key step is to measure the discrepancy between teacher and student networks with predefined distance functions. However, using the same distance for graphs of various structures may be unfit, and the optimal distance formulation is hard to determine. To tackle these problems, we propose a novel Adversarial Knowledge Distillation framework for graph models named GraphAKD, which adversarially trains a discriminator and a generator to adaptively detect and decrease the discrepancy. Specifically, noticing that the well-captured inter-node and inter-class correlations favor the success of deep GNNs, we propose to criticize the inherited knowledge from node-level and class-level views with a trainable discriminator. The discriminator distinguishes between teacher knowledge and what the student inherits, while the student GNN works as a generator and aims to fool the discriminator. To our best knowledge, GraphAKD is the first to introduce adversarial training to knowledge distillation in graph domains. Experiments on node-level and graph-level classification benchmarks demonstrate that GraphAKD improves the student performance by a large margin. The results imply that GraphAKD can precisely transfer knowledge from a complicated teacher GNN to a compact student GNN.

papers_seen.author: Martin

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful model compression technique used to create smaller, more efficient "student" neural networks that learn from larger, pre-trained "teacher" models. This process enables the deployment of complex deep learning models in resource-constrained environments, such as mobile devices. The core idea is to transfer the knowledge from a cumbersome teacher to a compact student, allowing the student to achieve performance that surpasses what it could by training on data alone. This technique has been successfully applied across diverse domains, including computer vision for tasks like object detection and image generation, and natural language processing for compressing large language models used in question answering and machine translation. Research continues to refine the distillation process through methods like using ensembles of teachers, selectively choosing what knowledge to transfer, and even training teachers to be more effective instructors for their students, thereby improving both model efficiency and performance.

papers_seen.title: Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: It is challenging to perform lifelong language learning (LLL) on a stream of different tasks without any performance degradation comparing to the multi-task counterparts. To address this issue, we present Lifelong Language Knowledge Distillation (L2KD), a simple but efficient method that can be easily applied to existing LLL architectures in order to mitigate the degradation. Specifically, when the LLL model is trained on a new task, we assign a teacher model to first learn the new task, and pass the knowledge to the LLL model via knowledge distillation. Therefore, the LLL model can better adapt to the new task while keeping the previously learned knowledge. Experiments show that the proposed L2KD consistently improves previous state-of-the-art models, and the degradation comparing to multi-task models in LLL tasks is well mitigated for both sequence generation and text classification tasks.

papers_seen.title: Ensemble Distillation for Neural Machine Translation
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation describes a method for training a student network to perform better by learning from a stronger teacher network. Translating a sentence with an Neural Machine Translation (NMT) engine is time expensive and having a smaller model speeds up this process. We demonstrate how to transfer the translation quality of an ensemble and an oracle BLEU teacher network into a single NMT system. Further, we present translation improvements from a teacher network that has the same architecture and dimensions of the student network. As the training of the student model is still expensive, we introduce a data filtering method based on the knowledge of the teacher model that not only speeds up the training, but also leads to better translation quality. Our techniques need no code change and can be easily reproduced with any NMT architecture to speed up the decoding process.

papers_seen.abstract: A critical challenge of federated learning is data heterogeneity and imbalance across clients, which leads to inconsistency between local networks and unstable convergence of global models. To alleviate the limitations, we propose a novel architectural regularization technique that constructs multiple auxiliary branches in each local model by grafting local and global subnetworks at several different levels and that learns the representations of the main pathway in the local model congruent to the auxiliary hybrid pathways via online knowledge distillation. The proposed technique is effective to robustify the global model even in the non-iid setting and is applicable to various federated learning frameworks conveniently without incurring extra communication costs. We perform comprehensive empirical studies and demonstrate remarkable performance gains in terms of accuracy and efficiency compared to existing methods. The source code is available at our project page.

papers_seen.abstract: Recent neural methods for vehicle routing problems always train and test the deep models on the same instance distribution (i.e., uniform). To tackle the consequent cross-distribution generalization concerns, we bring the knowledge distillation to this field and propose an Adaptive Multi-Distribution Knowledge Distillation (AMDKD) scheme for learning more generalizable deep models. Particularly, our AMDKD leverages various knowledge from multiple teachers trained on exemplar distributions to yield a light-weight yet generalist student model. Meanwhile, we equip AMDKD with an adaptive strategy that allows the student to concentrate on difficult distributions, so as to absorb hard-to-master knowledge more effectively. Extensive experimental results show that, compared with the baseline neural methods, our AMDKD is able to achieve competitive results on both unseen in-distribution and out-of-distribution instances, which are either randomly synthesized or adopted from benchmark datasets (i.e., TSPLIB and CVRPLIB). Notably, our AMDKD is generic, and consumes less computational resources for inference.

papers_seen.abstract: Despite Generative Adversarial Networks (GANs) have been widely used in various image-to-image translation tasks, they can be hardly applied on mobile devices due to their heavy computation and storage cost. Traditional network compression methods focus on visually recognition tasks, but never deal with generation tasks. Inspired by knowledge distillation, a student generator of fewer parameters is trained by inheriting the low-level and high-level information from the original heavy teacher generator. To promote the capability of student generator, we include a student discriminator to measure the distances between real images, and images generated by student and teacher generators. An adversarial learning process is therefore established to optimize student generator and student discriminator. Qualitative and quantitative analysis by conducting experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that the proposed method can learn portable generative models with strong performance.

papers_seen.author: Hernandez
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a crucial technique in deep learning, primarily for model compression. This process involves training a smaller, efficient 'student' model to replicate the performance of a larger, more complex 'teacher' model. By transferring the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, including nuanced probability distributions and internal feature representations, the student can achieve comparable or even superior performance with significantly fewer computational resources. While its primary application is creating compact models suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices, the utility of knowledge distillation extends further. It has been successfully applied to enhance model robustness, improve algorithmic fairness, facilitate domain adaptation, and increase model interpretability, making it a highly versatile and powerful tool for developing practical and efficient deep learning systems.

papers_seen.author: Smith
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Framework for Model Compression and Beyond
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to transfer knowledge from a large, complex 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The primary objective is to create compact models that retain the high performance of the teacher, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. This is typically achieved by training the student to mimic the teacher's outputs or internal feature representations. While initially conceived for compression, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded significantly. The framework is now used to enhance student model performance, sometimes even surpassing the teacher, and to address critical considerations like algorithmic fairness and data privacy. Its versatility has led to successful applications across diverse domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and recommender systems, establishing it as a multifaceted tool in modern machine learning.

papers_seen.author: Bernard
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Deep Learning Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique used to transfer knowledge from a large, complex model, known as the 'teacher', to a smaller, more efficient model, called the 'student'. This process enables the creation of compact neural networks that are suitable for deployment on resource-constrained devices without a significant loss in performance. The core idea is to train the student model to mimic the output distribution of the teacher model, leveraging the rich, learned information contained in the teacher's predictions. Variations of this technique include using multiple teachers, distilling knowledge from intermediate feature layers, and even training teacher models to be more 'student-friendly'. Knowledge distillation has found wide application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, as well as in specialized paradigms like federated learning to preserve privacy and improve communication efficiency.

This method has been successfully applied across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, to create compact models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts while being significantly faster and smaller.

papers_seen.author: Joyce
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation and Model Compression in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: The increasing size and complexity of deep learning models, particularly in natural language processing, pose significant challenges for their deployment in resource-constrained or latency-sensitive environments. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a prominent model compression technique to address these issues. This method involves transferring knowledge from a large, cumbersome "teacher" model to a smaller, more efficient "student" model. Various advanced strategies have been developed to enhance this process, including using multiple teachers, employing adversarial learning, and enabling the teacher to learn how to teach via meta-learning. The applications of knowledge distillation are diverse, extending from compressing large language models and enabling efficient graph-based inference to facilitating federated learning across heterogeneous devices. These techniques allow for the creation of smaller, faster models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making state-of-the-art deep learning more accessible for real-world applications.

papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression in deep learning and natural language processing. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. The primary objective is to create smaller, more computationally efficient models that retain the high performance of their larger counterparts, making them suitable for deployment in resource-constrained environments such as mobile devices. Knowledge is typically transferred by training the student to replicate the teacher's output probabilities or internal feature representations. The versatility of this framework is demonstrated by its broad application and its evolution into more advanced methods, including data-free distillation and self-distillation, which extend its utility beyond simple compression to areas like performance enhancement and improved generalization.

papers_seen.author: Reid
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression in deep learning, addressing the challenge of deploying large models in resource-constrained settings. This method employs a teacher-student framework, where knowledge is transferred from a large, pre-trained 'teacher' model to a smaller, more efficient 'student' model. The student is trained to mimic the rich outputs or internal representations of the teacher, enabling it to achieve comparable performance with a significantly smaller computational and memory footprint. This paradigm has proven highly effective and versatile, facilitating the practical application of state-of-the-art architectures in domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Bell
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the deployment challenges of large, computationally expensive models. It operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich knowledge learned by the teacher, enabling the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer parameters and lower computational costs. The primary goal is to create compact models suitable for resource-constrained environments. Beyond simple size reduction, the applications of knowledge distillation have expanded to include performance enhancement and the development of more efficient artificial intelligence systems for real-world scenarios.

papers_seen.author: Chambers
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a powerful technique in deep learning for compressing large, complex models into smaller, more efficient versions. This process operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior and performance of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary goal is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher, enabling the deployment of high-performing models in resource-constrained environments. By learning from the teacher's outputs or internal representations, the student can achieve comparable accuracy with a significantly smaller computational footprint. The applications of this versatile framework extend beyond simple compression to include performance enhancement, data privacy, and knowledge transfer across different domains like natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Morris
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation for Model Compression in Deep Learning and NLP
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a model compression technique in deep learning that addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a smaller, more efficient student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. The primary objective is to transfer the rich knowledge from the teacher to the student, creating compact, high-performance models suitable for resource-constrained environments like mobile devices. While initially focused on reducing model size and latency, the applications of this versatile technique have expanded to include enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and transferring knowledge across various domains such as natural language processing and computer vision.

papers_seen.author: Hill
papers_seen.title: A Deep Hierarchical Approach to Lifelong Learning in Minecraft
papers_seen.abstract: We propose a lifelong learning system that has the ability to reuse and transfer knowledge from one task to another while efficiently retaining the previously learned knowledge-base. Knowledge is transferred by learning reusable skills to solve tasks in Minecraft, a popular video game which is an unsolved and high-dimensional lifelong learning problem. These reusable skills, which we refer to as Deep Skill Networks, are then incorporated into our novel Hierarchical Deep Reinforcement Learning Network (H-DRLN) architecture using two techniques: (1) a deep skill array and (2) skill distillation, our novel variation of policy distillation (Rusu et. al. 2015) for learning skills. Skill distillation enables the HDRLN to efficiently retain knowledge and therefore scale in lifelong learning, by accumulating knowledge and encapsulating multiple reusable skills into a single distilled network. The H-DRLN exhibits superior performance and lower learning sample complexity compared to the regular Deep Q Network (Mnih et. al. 2015) in sub-domains of Minecraft.

papers_seen.author: Holland
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation as a Framework for Model Compression and Enhancement
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation is a prominent model compression technique in deep learning designed to address the challenge of deploying large, computationally intensive models in resource-constrained environments. The method operates on a teacher-student framework, where a smaller, more compact student model is trained to mimic the behavior of a larger, pre-trained teacher model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly reduced computational and memory costs. While its primary application is creating lightweight models, the utility of knowledge distillation extends to enhancing model performance, improving robustness, and enabling novel learning paradigms, making it a foundational tool in modern artificial intelligence.

papers_seen.author: Bowman
papers_seen.title: TRILLsson: Distilled Universal Paralinguistic Speech Representations
papers_seen.abstract: Recent advances in self-supervision have dramatically improved the quality of speech representations. However, deployment of state-of-the-art embedding models on devices has been restricted due to their limited public availability and large resource footprint. Our work addresses these issues by publicly releasing a collection of paralinguistic speech models that are small and near state-of-the-art performance. Our approach is based on knowledge distillation, and our models are distilled on public data only. We explore different architectures and thoroughly evaluate our models on the Non-Semantic Speech (NOSS) benchmark. Our largest distilled model is less than 15% the size of the original model (314MB vs 2.2GB), achieves over 96% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks, and is trained on 6.5% the data. The smallest model is 1% in size (22MB) and achieves over 90% the accuracy on 6 of 7 tasks. Our models outperform the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 model on 6 of 7 tasks, and our smallest model outperforms the open source Wav2Vec 2.0 on both emotion recognition tasks despite being 7% the size.

papers_seen.author: Christian
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Deep Learning Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a critical and versatile framework for model compression in deep learning. This technique addresses the challenge of deploying large, computationally expensive models in resource-constrained environments by operating on a teacher-student paradigm. A smaller, more efficient 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, enabling the creation of compact models that retain high performance while being significantly smaller and faster. Its success across numerous domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, has established it as a foundational tool for developing efficient and practical artificial intelligence systems.

papers_seen.author: Mckay
papers_seen.title: MixKD: Towards Efficient Distillation of Large-scale Language Models
papers_seen.abstract: Large-scale language models have recently demonstrated impressive empirical performance. Nevertheless, the improved results are attained at the price of bigger models, more power consumption, and slower inference, which hinder their applicability to low-resource (both memory and computation) platforms. Knowledge distillation (KD) has been demonstrated as an effective framework for compressing such big models. However, large-scale neural network systems are prone to memorize training instances, and thus tend to make inconsistent predictions when the data distribution is altered slightly. Moreover, the student model has few opportunities to request useful information from the teacher model when there is limited task-specific data available. To address these issues, we propose MixKD, a data-agnostic distillation framework that leverages mixup, a simple yet efficient data augmentation approach, to endow the resulting model with stronger generalization ability. Concretely, in addition to the original training examples, the student model is encouraged to mimic the teacher's behavior on the linear interpolation of example pairs as well. We prove from a theoretical perspective that under reasonable conditions MixKD gives rise to a smaller gap between the generalization error and the empirical error. To verify its effectiveness, we conduct experiments on the GLUE benchmark, where MixKD consistently leads to significant gains over the standard KD training, and outperforms several competitive baselines. Experiments under a limited-data setting and ablation studies further demonstrate the advantages of the proposed approach.

papers_seen.author: Rocha
papers_seen.title: Few Shot Network Compression via Cross Distillation
papers_seen.abstract: Model compression has been widely adopted to obtain light-weighted deep neural networks. Most prevalent methods, however, require fine-tuning with sufficient training data to ensure accuracy, which could be challenged by privacy and security issues. As a compromise between privacy and performance, in this paper we investigate few shot network compression: given few samples per class, how can we effectively compress the network with negligible performance drop? The core challenge of few shot network compression lies in high estimation errors from the original network during inference, since the compressed network can easily over-fits on the few training instances. The estimation errors could propagate and accumulate layer-wisely and finally deteriorate the network output. To address the problem, we propose cross distillation, a novel layer-wise knowledge distillation approach. By interweaving hidden layers of teacher and student network, layer-wisely accumulated estimation errors can be effectively reduced.The proposed method offers a general framework compatible with prevalent network compression techniques such as pruning. Extensive experiments on benchmark datasets demonstrate that cross distillation can significantly improve the student network's accuracy when only a few training instances are available.

papers_seen.author: Cochran
papers_seen.title: Knowledge Distillation: A Versatile Framework for Efficient Model Compression
papers_seen.abstract: Modern deep learning models have achieved unprecedented performance but their immense size and computational cost often hinder practical deployment. Knowledge distillation has emerged as a powerful model compression framework to address this challenge. It operates on a teacher-student paradigm, where a compact 'student' model is trained to mimic the behavior and outputs of a larger, pre-trained 'teacher' model. This process transfers the rich, generalized knowledge from the teacher, allowing the student to achieve comparable performance with significantly fewer resources. This makes it possible to deploy state-of-the-art models on devices with limited computational power, such as mobile phones. The technique's versatility is demonstrated by its broad application across various domains, including natural language processing and computer vision, and its adaptation into advanced methods like self-distillation and data-free distillation, further expanding its utility in developing efficient and robust AI systems.

papers_seen.author: Ramirez
papers_seen.title: Model Compression and Knowledge Distillation in Deep Learning
papers_seen.abstract: Knowledge distillation has emerged as a key technique for model compression, enabling the deployment of large, complex deep learning models on resource-constrained devices. This process involves transferring knowledge from a large, pre-trained "teacher" model to a smaller "student" model, aiming to replicate the teacher's performance with significantly fewer computational resources. This approach is applied across various domains, including natural language processing, computer vision, and graph neural networks, to create models that are smaller, faster, and more efficient. Research has explored numerous variations, such as self-distillation, multi-teacher distillation, and data-free methods that address challenges like data privacy and availability. Knowledge distillation is often combined with other compression techniques like pruning and quantization to further optimize model efficiency, striking a balance between performance and practicality.
